name: Petal brush
pitch: Draw a fingertip slowly through an open flower: the petals on your side fold away from the finger, a wisp of pollen in the flower's colour lifts from the pod and drifts downwind onto the water, and the flower sighs its note an octave up. Sweep through it fast and it flinches half-shut for a moment, rustles, and the crickets go quiet.
gesture: For each flower f with f.state === 'open' (at home, not held/adrift) and each hand h with h.visible && h.active && !h.pinch.active && !h.grabbed && !h.submerged, for k in 0..4: tip = h.tips[k]; in-petals when hypot(tip.x - f.bud.x, tip.z - f.bud.z) < 0.09 * f.scale and -0.03 <= tip.y - f.bud.y <= 0.07. v = h.joints[TIP_NAMES[k]].velocity.length() (rig-local m/s). While any tip is in the petals: f.pushDir = normalize((tip - f.bud).xz), f.push eases toward 0.40 rad with tau 0.12 s, and back to 0 with tau 0.5 s when no tip is inside. Brush event: 0.04 <= v < 0.6 and t - f.brushT >= 0.35 -> f.brushT = t, spawn 6 + round(10 * smoothstep(0.04, 0.30, v)) pollen grains at f.bud, ctx.energy = min(1, ctx.energy + 0.02), emit 'lotusbrush' { index, note, pos: f.bud.clone(), hand: h, speed: v }. Flinch: v >= 0.8 and f.flinchT <= 0 -> f.flinchT = 3.5, emit 'lotusflinch' { index, pos, hand, speed }, and every live pollen grain within 0.4 m of the tip gets vel += dir * 1.2. While flinchT > 0: shape = smoothstep(0, 0.25, 3.5 - flinchT) * (1 - smoothstep(0.25, 3.5, 3.5 - flinchT)); rendered bloom = 1 - 0.75 * shape, glow gain * (1 - 0.6 * shape); f.state stays 'open' and f.timer keeps running; the all-six chord test must count a flinching flower as open (f.open && (f.bloom > 0.6 || f.flinchT > 0)) so a flinch cannot re-arm and re-fire 'lotuschord'.
visual: Petal parting: one new per-instance attribute aPush (vec3: world-space push direction xz, magnitude in radians; InstancedBufferAttribute, DynamicDrawUsage, 6 instances) on flowerGeo. In LOTUS_FLOWER_VERT after radialDir: vec2 rw = normalize((mat3(instanceMatrix) * radialDir).xz); float side = max(dot(rw, aPush.xy), 0.0); theta0 += aPush.z * side * side * mix(0.7, 1.0, outer); kappa -= 0.25 * aPush.z * side; -> petals on the finger's side fold outward, the far side is untouched (4 lines, 0 draw calls). Pollen: one THREE.Points over a 192-slot pool in the drips.js pattern (Float32Array pos/vel/age/life/bright/colour rgb, Uint8 state, Int16 free list, no per-frame allocation), shader POLLEN_VERT/FRAG added to src/shaders/lotus.js: dead slots collapsed out of clip space like DRIPS_VERT, perspective size uSize 0.010 m capped at 18 px, fragment = glowSoft alpha * per-grain aColor, additive, renderOrder 4, depthWrite false, points.visible = live > 0. Grain motion: spawn at bud + 2 cm jitter, vel = 0.06 * (rnd-0.5) horizontal + 0.05 up; per frame vel += (wind * 0.08 - vel * 0.6) * dt with wind = ctx.shore.wind (unit Vector2, fallback (-0.7, 0.7)), plus 0.03 * sin(t * 1.7 + seed * 40) wander, vy -= 0.02 * dt; life 7-11 s, brightness fades over the last 40 %; a grain reaching y <= level + 0.002 sticks to the surface (state FLOAT: y = level + 0.002, drifts at wind * 0.05, fades over 5 s) so the water is dusted. Draw calls: +1 only while grains live. Per frame O(live <= 192).
sound: 'lotusbrush' -> sfx.js: noiseBurst(pink, bandpass 2200 Hz, Q 2, dur 0.18, gain 0.04 + 0.07 * smoothstep(0.04, 0.30, speed), refDistance 1.2) at pos (a sigh) + triggerBell({ midi: pitchFor(note, 6), pos, gain 0.07, dur 1.4, index 0.6, attack 0.03, wet 0.4, tag 'brush' }) and notePlayed (the aurora voice can quote it). 'lotusflinch' -> sfx.js: noiseBurst(white, bandpass 900 Hz, Q 1.5, dur 0.12, gain 0.10) (petals rustling); ambience.js: startle(2, 4) next to the existing lotuschord line. music: nothing.
discoverability: The petals visibly fold away from any finger that enters an open flower, so poking one already shows the reaction. Hint in hints.js: { id: 'brush', text: 'draw a finger slowly through an open flower', after: 130, ready: (ctx, s) => s.bloomed && ctx.lotus.nearestOpenDistance < REACH + 0.15, done: (ctx, s) => s.brushed } with s.brushed set from 'lotusbrush' and a new ctx.lotus.nearestOpenDistance (horizontal head distance to the nearest flower with state 'open', computed in the existing nearest-bud pass).
conflicts: A pinching hand is ignored entirely, so carrying a lantern or pulling the world through a flower changes nothing; closed buds keep the touch rule (bloom < 0.25) and open flowers use this one, so the two never overlap in time; no two-hand pose, so the leave gesture (two pinch-free palms together at chest height) cannot resemble it; fireflies want a still hand and brushing is 0.04-0.6 m/s (a landed firefly is only shaken off above 0.35 m/s, consistent with existing behaviour); the flinch threshold 0.8 m/s sits above the fireflies' repel threshold 0.7, so a fast hand startles both at once, which is the same rule the world already has.
harnessStep: After the existing lotus-bloomed step (flower B open; frames(60) so bloom = 1): for i in 0..36 { setHand('right', [B.x + 0.10 - 0.20 * i / 36, B.y + 0.07, B.z + 0.16], 0); frame() } — the index tip crosses the pod at ~0.2 m/s inside the 0.09 m petal radius. Assert: events().some(e => e.type === 'lotusbrush' && e.detail.index === B.index && e.detail.hand === 'right'); page.evaluate(() => window.__nocturneCtx.lotus.pollen.count) > 0; stats().drawCalls <= baseline + 1. Flinch: page.evaluate(() => window.__nocturneCtx.lotus.open(2)); frames(80); sweep 0.24 m across flower 2's pod in 7 frames (~1.2 m/s); assert 'lotusflinch' in events(), world().lotus[2].bloom < 0.5 within 10 frames, > 0.9 after frames(150), and stats().lotusOpen unchanged. Add 'lotusbrush','lotusflinch' to the main.js eventLog list and ctx.lotus.pollen = { count, spawned } to stats().
risks: Tip velocity is lerped 0.5/frame and rig-local, so the first sample of a slow stroke can read under 0.04 — rely on the 0.35 s rate limit rather than a tight speed band. The petal push runs on ~1.3k vertices x 6 instances (negligible) but touches the vertex shader, so the harness must pass with no shader errors on both desktop and XR paths. Pollen must stay tiny (10 mm, <= 18 px) and in the flower's colour or it reads as fireflies. The chord logic must treat a flinch as still-open (see gesture) or a fast hand could farm 'lotuschord' swells.
angle: Lotus. Make the six flowers behave like living plants that notice hands: closed buds turn toward a slow hand and open for a patient one; open flowers part their petals around a gentle finger and shed glowing pollen (and flinch from a fast one); an open bloom can be pinched off its float, carried, breathed in, and set adrift until a new bud rises; and pollen carried on a fingertip opens the next bud in a blended colour with a two-note bloom. Everything rides on the existing lotus.js instances and attributes (one new Points pool for pollen, +1 draw call only while grains live), the existing grab protocol, and the event -> sfx/music/ambience pattern.

name: Buds that turn to the hand
pitch: Bring a hand near a closed bud and it leans toward your nearest fingertip, its faint glow warming as you get closer. Hold the finger still just above it — not touching — for two seconds and the bud opens on its own, with a thin rising whisper first and a softer, longer bloom note than a touch gives.
gesture: For each flower with f.state === 'closed' (bloom < 0.25, at home): over hands h with h.visible && h.active && !h.submerged && !h.pinch.active && !h.grabbed, take the nearest of h.tips[0..4] to f.bud (squared distances; 6 x 2 x 5 = 60 checks per frame). d = that distance. If d < 0.35: p = 1 - smoothstep(0.08, 0.35, d); lean axis = horizontal unit (tip - bud).xz; target angle 0.40 * p rad; f.leanX/f.leanZ ease toward the target with k = 1 - exp(-dt / 0.6) and decay with tau 1.2 s when no hand is within 0.35 m; closed-bud glow gain = 0.08 + 0.14 * p. Patience: if 0.09 <= d <= 0.22 && h.still (filtered palm displacement < 3 cm over 0.5 s) -> f.hoverT += dt, else f.hoverT = max(0, f.hoverT - 2 * dt). At f.hoverT >= 0.6 && !f.stirred: f.stirred = true, emit 'lotusstir' { index, note, pos: f.bud.clone(), hand: h }. At f.hoverT >= 2.0: openFlower(i, h, { patient: true }) — the normal 1.6 s bloom, energy +0.15, disturb(0.18, 0.28) and 'lotusbloom' { ..., patient: true }. hoverT and stirred reset on open or when hoverT reaches 0. Open, held and adrift flowers skip this block (parting in Petal brush is an open flower's answer). Lean magnitude is exposed as f.lean (= hypot(leanX, leanZ)) for the harness.
visual: No new geometry, 0 draw calls. The lean goes into the instance matrix: _q = quaternion(axis = (leanZ, 0, -leanX) / |lean|, angle |lean|) multiplied by the yaw quaternion; compose(f.position, _q, _s). The geometry origin is the base, so the flower pivots at the water line. f.bud = (0, BUD_HEIGHT * f.scale, 0).applyQuaternion(_q).add(f.position) every frame before the touch test, so the touch target and the glow quad (glowPos) follow the leaning pod. One quaternion multiply per flower per frame.
sound: 'lotusstir' -> sfx.js: noiseBurst(white, bandpass at 2 * mtof(pitchFor(note, 6)) Hz (~2.3-3.5 kHz), Q 14, dur 1.4, gain 0.035, sweepTo 1.5x, refDistance 1.0) at the bud — a thin rising whisper; if the hand leaves it simply finishes. 'lotusbloom' with patient === true -> onLotus uses attack 0.06, dur 4.2, gain 0.40 (a softer, longer bloom for a patient hand); everything else in onLotus unchanged. music/ambience: nothing.
discoverability: No hint. The bud visibly leans toward a hand from 35 cm and its glow warms as the hand nears, which is the invitation; stopping just short of a flower is what a careful person does anyway, and two seconds later it opens by itself. The existing 'the buds open when you touch them' hint is unchanged.
conflicts: No pinch and no two-hand pose are involved: pinch-pull hands are pinching and are ignored, the leave pose needs two pinch-free palms pressed together at chest height (nowhere near a bud, and the buds only react to fingertips). A submerged hand is ignored, so paddling under a bud never opens it. The existing touch rule (any tip within 8 cm) still wins if the hand keeps descending. A hovering open still hand also attracts fireflies — both are rewards for stillness and they simply happen together (fireflies land on the hand as the bud opens), not a contradiction.

Negative check on another bud: setHand at d = 0.30 for frames(110) -> no 'lotusbloom' for that index. Add 'lotusstir' to the main.js eventLog list and 'patient' to summarize's key list.

name: Pick a bloom
pitch: Pinch the stem of an open flower and it comes away from its float, swaying in your fingers and glowing a little brighter; bring it to your face and it breathes out a puff of pollen while the harmony turns over. Let it go and it drifts down to the water with a soft plop, floats off on the wind for a minute, closes, sinks, and a new bud rises from the empty float.
gesture: Each flower gets a grabbable pushed to ctx.grabbables in init: { position: f.bud (live Vector3), radius: 0.05, active: f.state === 'open' || f.state === 'adrift', held: null, warm: false, kind: 'lotus', flower: f, onGrab(hand), onRelease(hand, velocity, { lost }) }. hands.js does the rest: a tip pinch (thumb-index < 0.020 m for 2 frames) whose pinch.point is within 0.05 + grabRadius 0.13 = 0.18 m of the pod grabs it (a lantern nearer to the same pinch point wins, as today), or a whole-hand grasp (meanCurl > 0.75) whose palm is within 0.23 m. onGrab: f.state = 'held', f.held = hand, f.stayPaused = true, emit 'lotuspluck' { index, note, pos: f.bud.clone(), hand }. Held, per frame: base position = hand.pinch.point + (0, -0.02, 0) (the stem pinched just under the pod), sway lean = clamp(-palm.velocityLocal.xz * 0.25, 0.5 rad) eased tau 0.15 s, bloom 1, glow gain x 1.3. Breathe: if hand.pinch.point.distanceTo(ctx.playerCtl.state.headWorld) < 0.22 && t - f.breatheT >= 6 -> f.breatheT = t, f.surge = 1 (decays over 2 s; glow gain x (1 + 1.5 * surge)), 12 pollen grains from the pod if the Petal-brush pool exists, ctx.energy = min(1, energy + 0.05), emit 'lotusbreathe' { index, note, pos, hand }. onRelease(hand, velocity, { lost }): f.state = 'falling', vel = lost ? 0 : velocity * 0.3 (clamped to 0.6 m/s), spin (rnd - 0.5) * 1.5 rad/s; per frame vy -= 9.81 * dt, horizontal vel *= max(0, 1 - 3 * dt), vy = max(vy, -0.45) (petals drag); when base y <= level + swell(x, z, t) + FLOWER_LIFT (or it was released under water) -> f.state = 'adrift': y eases to the surface with tau 0.3 s, ctx.water.disturb(x, z, 0.10, 0.12 + 0.2 * min(1, |vy| / 0.45)), emit 'lotusfloat' { index, note, pos: f.position.clone(), speed: |vy| }. Adrift: drift = ctx.shore.wind * 0.045 + random walk (walk target re-picked every 3-8 s, +-0.02 m/s, eased) + the lanterns' head-avoidance push (0.42 m), bloom 1 for adriftStay 40-60 s, then closes over CLOSE_SECONDS 6, then 'sinking' 3 s (y -= 0.10 * smoothstep), then 'regrow': x/z snap to home under the surface, y rises from -0.10 to FLOWER_LIFT over 4 s, scale 0.6 -> f.scale, bloom 0 -> f.state = 'closed' (touchable again, chord logic sees it as closed throughout). An adrift bloom is grabbable again (active includes 'adrift'), so it can be fetched back out of the water. Touch-open, lean and brush blocks skip any flower whose state is not at home.
visual: The same flowerMesh instance moves (0 draw calls). The little green float (geometry part 3) must stay behind: add a per-instance aHome vec3 attribute (DynamicDrawUsage; home x, level + swell + FLOWER_LIFT, home z written each frame) and in LOTUS_FLOWER_VERT for part > 2.5: wp = vec4(local * length(instanceMatrix[0].xyz) + aHome, 1.0); nW = nLocal; (6 lines) — pod and petals lift off, the float keeps bobbing, and during regrow the new bud rises out of the water beside it. The glow quad and its mirror already follow f.bud; the mirror shader handles a bud above or on the water. world() lotus entries gain state: f.state.
sound: 'lotuspluck' -> sfx.js: noiseBurst(pink, bandpass 700 Hz, Q 2, dur 0.05, gain 0.08) (a soft stem snap) + triggerBell({ midi: pitchFor(note, 5), pos, gain 0.2, dur 1.2, index 1.0, kind 'glass', tag 'pluck' }) — the note, plucked. 'lotusbreathe' -> sfx.js: triggerBell({ midi: pitchFor(note, 4), pos, gain 0.14, dur 3.5, attack 0.08, wet 0.8, kind 'ceramic' }) — a low wet bloom at the face; music.js: ctx.events.on('lotusbreathe', () => ctx.music.advance()) — the chord turns over (no-op while the pads are breathing). Nothing continuous while held; the crackle slots stay with the lanterns.
discoverability: Anyone who has lifted a lantern will try pinching a glowing flower. Hint in hints.js: { id: 'pick', text: 'pinch an open flower to pick it', after: 110, ready: (ctx, s) => s.bloomed && s.grabbed && ctx.lotus.nearestOpenDistance < REACH + 0.15, done: (ctx, s) => s.plucked } with s.plucked set from 'lotuspluck'. name: Pollen on the fingers
pitch: After brushing an open flower your fingertip carries a few glowing specks of its colour; dip that finger in the lake and they float off as dust, or touch a different closed bud with it and that bud opens in a blend of the two colours, ringing two notes instead of one. Nothing is explained: it is what pollen does.
gesture: Builds on Petal brush (needs its pool and 'lotusbrush'). Per hand hi (0 left, 1 right): pollen[hi] (Float32Array(2)), pollenFrom[hi] (Int8Array, -1), pollenColor[hi] (Color). On a brush by hand hi of flower f: pollen[hi] = min(1, pollen[hi] + 0.5), pollenFrom[hi] = f.index, pollenColor[hi].copy(f.color); pin 5 grains from the pool to that hand (state PINNED: each frame position = h.tips[0] + a fixed per-grain 6 mm jitter, colour = the flower's). Per frame pollen[hi] -= dt / 25; at <= 0 the pinned grains are released as ordinary drifting grains and pollenFrom[hi] = -1. If h.enteredWater (one-frame edge from hands.js) && pollen[hi] > 0.05: the pinned grains detach to the surface (FLOAT state at level + 0.002, drifting with the wind, fading over 5 s), emit 'lotusdust' { pos: h.tips[0].clone(), hand: h }, pollen[hi] = 0. Pollination: openFlower(i, hand, opts) (the touch loop and the patient-open path pass the hand): if hand && pollen[hi] > 0.25 && pollenFrom[hi] !== i && pollenFrom[hi] >= 0: f.color.copy(native[i]).lerp(pollenColor[hi], 0.5), write colorAttr.setXYZ(i) and glowColArr[i*3..] and set needsUpdate, f.note2 = flowers[pollenFrom[hi]].note, emit 'lotusbloom' { index, note, note2, pollen: pollenFrom[hi], pos, color, hand, patient? }, pollen[hi] = 0 and its pinned grains burst from the new flower (vel 0.3 outward). When that flower next reaches state 'closed' its colour reverts to CONFIG.colors.lotus[i % 6] and note2 is cleared. Hands are read only for tips[0], enteredWater and the hand passed into openFlower; no pinch, curl or stillness fields.
visual: 0 draw calls: the specks are grains from the Petal-brush pool pinned to the index tip (they ride the finger visibly at 10 mm, in the flower's colour); the water where the finger dipped is dusted with them; the pollinated flower opens in a blended colour (pink x mint, amber x violet, ...) because aColor (make the InstancedBufferAttribute DynamicDrawUsage) and the glow colour array are updated for that instance. The lotus fragment shader already derives petal, pod and halo colour from aColor, so the whole flower — pod glow, petal self-glow, halo and mirrored halo — changes together.
sound: 'lotusbloom' with a numeric note2 -> onLotus in sfx.js plays a second bell 120 ms after the first: triggerBell({ midi: pitchFor(note2, 5), pos, gain 0.32, dur 3.2, kind: the opposite of the first (ceramic if the first was glass), when: now + 0.12, tag 'lotus' }); the tuned bowl/ting layer only on the first. Both notes pass pitchFor's nearestConsonant, so the dyad is consonant with the current chord by construction; both go to notePlayed so the aurora voice can quote the pair. 'lotusdust' -> sfx.js: 3 highpass ticks at 2800 Hz, dur 0.012, gain 0.03, 35 ms apart (the plankton taking the dust). music/ambience: nothing new — the bloom still fires the normal lotusbloom path, chord and energy logic unchanged.
discoverability: No hint; it is emergent and needs none. After a brush the finger visibly glows with specks, so the next thing touched with that finger reveals what they do; the existing lotus and brush hints lead here. Because charge decays over 25 s, the chain works within a normal reach from cluster 0 to the next cluster.
conflicts: It has no gesture of its own: it piggybacks on Petal brush (moving fingertip in an open flower) and the existing touch-open, neither of which reads pinch or two-hand poses, so pinch-pull locomotion, grabbing and the leave gesture are untouched. The hand-enter edge is only consumed cosmetically; handenter's own sweep sound and the drips module still fire. Fireflies are unaffected — a firefly may sit on a pollen-dusted finger. The pollinated bloom is still a 'lotusbloom', so hints, chord and energy behave exactly as before.
harnessStep: After the Petal-brush step (flower B brushed by the right hand): assert page.evaluate(() => window.__nocturneCtx.lotus.pollen.onHand[1]) > 0.4. Within 20 s of scenario time, pick a closed bud C !== B from world().lotus (e.g. flower 1 at 1.4-3.8 m — setHand takes world coordinates, so reach is not an issue for the fake hand). setHand('right', [C.x, C.y + 0.3, C.z + 0.16], 0); frames(10); descend 20 frames to C.y + 0.06; frames(30). Assert the newest 'lotusbloom' has detail.index === C.index, detail.pollen === B.index and typeof detail.note2 === 'number', and page.evaluate((i) => window.__nocturneCtx.lotus.flowers[i].color.getHex(), C.index) !== CONFIG.colors.lotus[C.index % 6]. angle: Lotus. Make the six flowers behave like living plants that notice hands: closed buds turn toward a slow hand and open for a patient one; open flowers part their petals around a gentle finger and shed glowing pollen (and flinch from a fast one); an open bloom can be pinched off its float, carried, breathed in, and set adrift until a new bud rises; and pollen carried on a fingertip opens the next bud in a blended colour with a two-note bloom. Everything rides on the existing lotus.js instances and attributes (one new Points pool for pollen, +1 draw call only while grains live), the existing grab protocol, and the event -> sfx/music/ambience pattern.

name: Touch and nudge
pitch: Reach out and lay a hand against a floating lantern and it gives: a slow hand rests it against your fingers where it nuzzles, a brisk sideways brush sends it gliding off with a slow spin, its flame leaning and guttering in the wind of your hand, and a ring spreading from the hull. Nothing to learn: the first thing everyone does is try to touch one, and today the hand passes straight through.
gesture: Per hand h with h.visible && h.active && !h.pinch.active && !h.grasp && !h.grabbed (a grasp within 30 cm already grabs via the existing grasp rule, so a fist never reaches here; a pinching hand is grabbing or pulling the world). Pre-filter lanterns L with L.state === 'floating' && !L.dropping && h.palm.position.distanceToSquared(L.position) < 0.45*0.45 (at most 3-4 lanterns). Contact points: h.joints[n] for n in ['wrist','middle-finger-metacarpal','index-finger-phalanx-proximal','middle-finger-phalanx-proximal','ring-finger-phalanx-proximal','pinky-finger-phalanx-proximal', ...TIP_NAMES] with j.valid; effective radius jr = j.radius + 0.008. Vertical band: L.position.y - 0.11 < j.position.y < L.top.y - 0.02 (the paper flank only; a palm resting on the top rim never pushes, which keeps the shading feature clean). Horizontal d = hypot(j.position.x - L.position.x, j.position.z - L.position.z); contact if d < 0.075 + jr. Resolution: pen = 0.075 + jr - d, n = (dx, dz)/d from joint to lantern; L.position.x += n.x*pen, L.position.z += n.z*pen (positional, no vertical push). Velocity transfer with the world palm velocity: vn = max(0, h.palm.velocity.x*n.x + h.palm.velocity.z*n.z); new Vector2 L.push (allocated at spawn): if vn*0.9 > push.dot(n) then push += n*(vn*0.9 - push.dot(n)), clamp |push| <= 0.7 m/s; tangential vt = palm.velocity - n*vn -> L.spinKick = clamp(L.spinKick + (n.x*vt.z - n.z*vt.x)*2.5*dt*30, -2.5, 2.5). Decay per frame: push *= max(0, 1 - 1.5*dt), spinKick *= max(0, 1 - 0.9*dt). In the floating branch: vx += push.x, vz += push.y; L.yaw += (L.spin + L.spinKick)*dt; L.leanT += push*0.5 (heels away). Flame: L.flame target 1 + min(0.7, |push|*1.2) while |push| > 0.05; gutter at a contact start with vn > 0.35: L.bright = max(0.3, L.bright - 0.2) (the existing 0.6/s easing restores it). Attraction ease-out so the nuzzle does not jitter: multiply the existing att pull by smoothstep(ad, 0.095, 0.175) where ad is the horizontal distance from h.pinch.point to L.position. Contact start = no contact for this lantern on the previous frame and t - L.touchT > 0.25: emit 'lanterntouch' { pos: L.position.clone(), hand: h, lantern: L, speed: vn }, L.touchT = t, ctx.water.disturb(L.position.x, L.position.z, 0.1, 0.05 + 0.2*min(1, vn)), ctx.lanterns.touches++. Held and rising lanterns are never pushed (the string holds them; this keeps the wish-tracing hand from swinging a held lantern).
visual: No new geometry. The push, spin and lean go through the existing instance matrix (L.yaw, L.lean via L.leanT), the flame flare through pFlame/aFlame on the flame quads, the gutter through aBright on bodies, glow and mirror; the water lights (uLights, bright*flame) and the hull ripple (already strength-scaled by hypot(vx,vz)) follow automatically. 0 extra draw calls, no per-frame allocation (L.push/L.spinKick live on the record; contact math on scalars and the module's tmp vectors).
sound: 'lanterntouch' -> sfx: noiseBurst({ pos: e.pos, dur: 0.05 + 0.05*sp, gain: 0.03 + 0.10*sp, type: 'bandpass', freq: 900, q: 1.2 }) with sp = clamp(e.speed/0.8, 0, 1): a soft paper tap, louder for a brisk brush, nothing for a sustained nuzzle (rate-limited by the 0.25 s contact-start rule). The crackle slot on that lantern rises by itself with L.flame (assignCrackle reads bright/flame every 0.5 s). music: nothing. ambience: nothing. Water: the disturb at contact makes the plankton glow and a ring at the hull.
discoverability: Inherent: hands already pass through lanterns and players reach for them within the first minute; the open-hand attraction (which stays) brings the lantern to the fingers, and the first contact answers with the tap, the ring and the leaning flame. No hint. Only hints.js is touched to keep the 'lantern' hint's done() as is (touching does not count as lifting).
conflicts: Never uses pinch: a pinching hand is excluded, so pinch-near-lantern still grabs and pinch-and-move still pulls the world. A grasp (meanCurl > 0.75) within 30 cm already grabs via hands.js graspNear before this code runs, so 'closed hand takes, open hand pushes' is consistent. Leave: palms together at the chest are inside the lantern avoidance radius (0.42 m from the head) so no lantern is there to push, and the leave detector ignores lanterns anyway. Fireflies: a fast hand (> 0.7 m/s) scatters fireflies and shoves lanterns, a slow one lets both settle; a still open hand with fireflies on the tips and a lantern nuzzling it is coherent. Water: submerged joints are outside the vertical band of a floating lantern's flank (the flank starts 11 cm below the centre, 1 cm below the surface), so paddling never flings lanterns.
harnessStep: After 'calibrated': w = world(); L = nearest floating lantern (world coords), L0 = [L.x, L.z]. Pose the right hand open (curl 0.05, pinch 0, pitchDeg 0, rollDeg 0, yawDeg 90 so the fingers extend along -X) at wrist [L.x + 0.32, L.y + 0.02, L.z]; frames(8). Sweep the wrist x from L.x + 0.32 to L.x + 0.05 over 20 frames (0.27 m in 0.56 s, about 0.5 m/s; the fingertips, 0.17 m ahead, pass through the body), sampling world() every 2 frames and keeping minX = min over samples of that lantern's x. frames(10). Assert: events() contains 'lanterntouch' with detail.speed > 0.2 and detail.hand === 'right'; minX < L0.x - 0.10 (pushed away along -X); stats().hands.pinchR === false and no 'pinchmiss'/'grab' since the step began; world().rig unchanged (< 0.005 m). Then move the hand 0.7 m up and out of the attraction band; frames(30); assert ctx.lanterns.touches >= 1 via window.__nocturneCtx and that the lantern's state is still 'floating'. Expose L.push length in world() lanterns entries as 'push' for the info payload.
risks: Jitter when the attraction pulls the lantern into a still hand while contact pushes it out (mitigated by positional resolution plus the smoothstep ease-out of att inside 0.175 m; tune the two radii together). Tunnelling: joint velocity is capped at 4 m/s, 5.5 cm per frame at 72 Hz against a 7.5 cm body, so a full-speed swipe can skip the flank on one frame; acceptable, a swipe that misses looks like a miss. Quest fingertip jitter (about 5 mm) against a resting hand produces micro-pushes: the 8 mm skin and the 0.25 s event rate hide it, and push only accumulates when vn > push.dot(n). A pushed lantern can drift out of reach; the existing homing (wantMore) brings it back. Palm velocity includes the rig velocity, which is right for pushing a world-space object while gliding.
angle: Lanterns as bodies with a flame. Every new act builds on the two things a lantern already does (it is pinched and carried on a string; it drifts toward an open hand) and on the per-instance bright/flame values the shaders, the water lights and the crackle already read, so none of it touches pinch or the two-hand vocabulary. In order of physical directness: an open hand can touch and nudge a floating lantern; a lit lantern held in the hand can pass its flame to a dark one (some arrivals now come dark, and a dark lantern has no lift); a palm laid over the top shades the flame, dims it, and held long enough puts it out; and while one hand holds a lantern the other index fingertip can trace a wish into its paper, which rises with it. Each adds zero draw calls (instance attributes, one small DataTexture) and only touches lanterns within arm's reach per frame.

name: Passing the flame
pitch: Some lanterns now come in from the far shore dark, a pale paper ghost on the water with no light in it, and a dark one that you lift has no warmth in your hand and simply drops back when you let it go. Hold a lit lantern and bring its flame slowly against the dark one's wick: the wick glows, then catches with a soft bloom of light, the water lights up under it, and now it too can be lifted and sent up.
gesture: New per-lantern fields: L.lit (bool, true by default), L.catch (0..1), L.grab.warm = L.lit. Dark lanterns: the last of the four ring lanterns spawned at 1.3-3.2 m in init (index 3 of that loop) starts dark; thereafter every third far arrival (s.arrivals counter incremented in spawnFar and respawnFar; dark when s.arrivals % 3 === 2). Dark = lit false, bright eased to 0.04, flame eased to 0, grab.warm false. Lighting, evaluated every frame only for held lit lanterns (at most 2): for each Lh with Lh.state === 'held' && Lh.lit and each Ld with !Ld.lit && Ld.state !== 'rising': flame points fh = Lh.position + (0,-0.05,0), fd = Ld.position + (0,-0.05,0) (tmp vectors), d = fh.distanceTo(fd). If d < 0.16: Ld.catch += dt/0.4; else Ld.catch = max(0, Ld.catch - dt/0.8) (warmth accumulates through the pendulum swing rather than resetting; a fast pass does not light it). Ember preview: while d < 0.30 the flame target for Ld is 0.35*smoothstep(0.30, 0.16, d) (a faint wick). While Ld.catch > 0 the 0.22 m lantern-lantern separation is skipped for the pair (the wicks are allowed to touch). At Ld.catch >= 1: Ld.lit = true, Ld.catch = 0, Ld.flame = 2.0 (eases to 1 at the existing 3/s), bright target BRIGHT_FLOAT reached at 1.2/s, Ld.grab.warm = true, ctx.energy = min(1, ctx.energy + 0.1), ctx.water.disturb(Ld.position.x, Ld.position.z, 0.12, 0.15), emit 'lanternlight' { pos: Ld.position.clone(), hand: Lh.held, lantern: Ld, from: Lh }, ctx.lanterns.lightings++. Brightness targets everywhere become target*(lit ? 1 : 0) + (lit ? 0 : 0.04): floating BRIGHT_FLOAT, held (tracked ? 1 : 0.6). onRelease for a dark lantern: if info.lost -> drop as today; else always setFloating(L, top above water ? 'drop' : true), never 'rising' (no flame, no lift; the existing dropping branch handles the fall and the 'lanternsplash'). Dark lanterns still float, drift, home toward the player and are attracted to open hands (they arrive as a mystery). The hand holding the lit lantern is doing nothing new: h.grabbed gates locomotion, so moving it slowly is never a pull. Test hook: ctx.lanterns.setLit(i, lit) applying the same transitions without the event; ctx.lanterns.nearestDarkDistance (horizontal, from headWorld) for the hint.
visual: Body shader (LANTERN_BODY_FRAG): I = mix(0.05, 1.7, vBright) instead of mix(0.25, ...) so bright 0.04 is a barely-lit paper, plus a starlit silhouette term col += vec3(0.035, 0.045, 0.06) * (0.4 + 0.6*ndv) * (1.0 - vBright) so a dark lantern reads as a pale ghost on the black water; flame quads: aFlame 0 collapses ws to 0 (already multiplied), glow and mirror already scale with aBright (0.04 is invisible). Catch flare: flame 2.0 -> 1 makes the 3 cm flame dot bloom to 6 cm for a second; bright ramping lights the paper from the inside and the water lights (uLights) pick it up at once. Rendering changes are 4 lines of GLSL; 0 extra draw calls, no allocations (dark/lit is a bool on the record).
sound: 'lanternlight' -> sfx: noiseBurst({ pos: e.pos, dur: 0.35, gain: 0.10, type: 'lowpass', freq: 300, sweepTo: 1400, kind: 'pink' }) (a soft fwoomp as the wick takes) then triggerBell({ midi: 60 + mod12(ctx.music.currentChord.fifth), pos: e.pos, kind: 'ceramic', gain: 0.22, dur: 3, attack: 0.03, when: now + 0.12, tag: 'lantern' }) and notePlayed; the crackle slot for that lantern rises with bright at the next 0.5 s assignCrackle (lanternAudible already mutes l.lit === false, so dark lanterns are silent today with no change). A dark lantern dropped from the hand plays the existing 'lanternsplash'. music: nothing new. ambience: nothing.
discoverability: The dark ring lantern homes in with the others in the first minutes; it is grabbable, cold in the hand (no warmth on the fingers) and drops when released, which says it is missing something. Hint in hints.js: { id: 'relight', text: 'touch a lit lantern to the dark one', after: 45, ready: (ctx, s) => s.grabbed && ctx.lanterns.nearestDarkDistance < REACH + 0.15 && ctx.lanterns.nearestDistance < REACH + 0.15, done: (ctx) => (ctx.lanterns.lightings || 0) > 0 }.
conflicts: Uses only an existing grab (the lit lantern is held by pinch as today) and slow motion of the held hand, which player.js never treats as a pull because h.grabbed is set. Pinching near a dark lantern grabs it exactly as before (radius and grabbable unchanged), so pinch near an object still grabs or does nothing. No two-hand pose is involved; a second hand may hold the dark one, and flame-to-flame between two held lanterns works the same way (the dark one's Ld.state === 'held' is allowed). Fireflies: unaffected; the lighting hand is pinching so it never attracts them. Leave: unaffected. Water: a held lantern dipped near the surface already floats on its slack string; the catch radius is measured between flame points so no submerged geometry is involved.
harnessStep: Add lit, bright and flame to world().lanterns entries and 'lanternlight' to the main.js event list. Step: after the existing 'lantern-grabbed' step (right hand holding lantern L with pinch 1), pick J = the second-nearest floating lantern within 1.6 m and call window.__nocturneCtx.lanterns.setLit(J.i, false); frames(6); assert world().lanterns[J.i].lit === false and bright < 0.1. Read p = ctx.hands.right.pinch.point; over 30 frames move the right wrist (pinch 1) by the delta that brings p to [J.x + 0.08, J.y + 0.21, J.z] (the held flame hangs 0.26 m below the pinch point: 0.08 string + 0.13 half height + 0.05 flame offset, so the two flames sit 8 cm apart); frames(40) (1.1 s > the 0.4 s dwell, with margin for the swing). Assert: events() contains 'lanternlight' with detail.hand === 'right'; world().lanterns[J.i].lit === true; after frames(60) bright > 0.3; stats().energy increased by >= 0.08 over the step; no 'lanternrelease' or 'pinchmiss' in the step. Negative: setLit(K.i, false) on a third lantern, release L, grab K (pinch at [K.x, K.y + 0.12, K.z]), lift 0.4 m over 24 frames, release; frames(60); assert a 'lanternsplash' for K, no 'lanternrelease', and world().lanterns[K.i].state === 'floating'.
risks: A dark lantern must stay visible at night or the feature is invisible: the silhouette term needs tuning against the fog and the moonless minutes (verify in a harness screenshot at 2 m). Players who drop a dark lantern from a height get a splash they did not expect; the hint and the cold hand explain it. The pendulum swing while holding the lit lantern moves the flame in and out of 0.16 m: the accumulate/decay catch handles it, but 0.4 s dwell versus 0.8 s decay should be tuned on the headset. Skipping the pair separation while catch > 0 lets the two bodies overlap briefly; visually fine for paper. Arrivals every third dark means at most one or two dark lanterns near the player at a time; never a dead end because lit arrivals keep coming and home in.

name: Shading the flame
pitch: Lay an open palm gently over the top of a lantern and the flame starves under it: the paper dims, the crackle goes muffled, the lantern stays sheltered under your hand. Lift the palm and the flame flares back with a soft whump; keep it there long enough and the light goes out with a hiss, leaving a dark lantern to be relit from another.
gesture: Per hand h with h.visible && h.active && h.open && !h.pinch.active && !h.grabbed && !h.submerged && h.palm.normal.y < -0.6 (palm facing down) && h.palm.speed < 0.35 (a laid-on hand, not a passing one). For each lantern L with L.lit && (L.state === 'floating' || (L.state === 'held' && L.held !== h)): dy = h.palm.position.y - L.top.y, dh = hypot(h.palm.position.x - L.top.x, h.palm.position.z - L.top.z); covered if 0 < dy < 0.07 && dh < 0.09. L.cover eases toward 1 with tau 0.5 s while covered, toward 0 with tau 0.3 s otherwise (a one-frame tracking hiccup does not break it). Effects while cover > 0: brightness target multiplied by (1 - 0.75*cover) (0.14 fully covered when floating), flame target 1 - 0.65*cover, and shelter: in the floating branch vx *= (1 - 0.85*cover), vz likewise, so the lantern stays under the palm instead of drifting out on the wind. L.coverFor += dt while cover > 0.8, else coverFor = max(0, coverFor - dt); ctx.lanterns.covers++ the first time cover exceeds 0.8 in an episode (L.coverEp flag). Snuff at coverFor >= 3.5: L.lit = false (same transition as the flame-passing feature: flame -> 0 over 0.3 s, bright -> 0.04, grab.warm false), emit 'lanternsnuff' { pos: L.position.clone(), hand: h, lantern: L }, ctx.lanterns.snuffs++, coverFor = 0. Flare: when cover falls below 0.3 with coverFor > 0.5 and L.lit: L.flame = 1.5 (eases back at 3/s), a 1 s brightness overshoot of +0.25 (L.flareT = t), emit 'lanternflare' { pos, lantern }. If built without the flame-passing feature, a snuffed lantern rekindles on its own 30-45 s later (ember: flame 0.3 for 2 s, then flame 1.6 -> 1, bright back to BRIGHT_FLOAT, emit 'lanternlight' with from: null); with it, a snuffed lantern stays dark until lit from another.
visual: No new geometry: cover drives the existing aBright (bodies/glow/mirror) and aFlame (flame quads), so the paper dims from the inside, the halo shrinks, the mirror on the water fades and the water lights (uLights = bright*flame) go out under the palm. The hand's own material already shows lantern warmth only when holding, so nothing to change there. 0 extra draw calls, no allocation (cover/coverFor/flareT are numbers on the record).
sound: Continuous: in assignCrackle, sl.level *= (1 - 0.85*(l.cover || 0)) and sl.bp.frequency.setTargetAtTime(2500 - 1300*cover, now, 0.2) so the crackle goes quiet and muffled under the palm (0.5 s cadence is fine against a 3.5 s starve). 'lanternsnuff' -> sfx noiseBurst({ pos, dur: 0.45, gain: 0.08, type: 'lowpass', freq: 1800, sweepTo: 300, kind: 'pink' }) (a hiss that falls), and the slot mutes via lanternAudible (l.lit === false). 'lanternflare' -> sfx noiseBurst({ pos, dur: 0.14, gain: 0.06, type: 'lowpass', freq: 400, sweepTo: 1600 }) (a soft whump) plus triggerBell({ midi: pitchFor(0, 6), pos, gain: 0.08, dur: 1.2, kind: 'glass' }), barely there. music: nothing. ambience: nothing (a snuff is too small to startle crickets).
discoverability: The flame already brightens when an open hand comes near (flame 1.3 while attracted), which invites hovering; the first time the palm rests over the top the dimming and muffled crackle answer within half a second. Late hint in hints.js for anyone who has lifted lanterns but never shaded one: { id: 'shade', text: 'shade the flame with your palm', after: 180, ready: (ctx, s) => s.grabbed && ctx.lanterns.nearestDistance < REACH, done: (ctx) => (ctx.lanterns.covers || 0) > 0 }.
conflicts: No pinch involved (a pinching or grabbing hand is excluded), so grabbing and pull-the-world are untouched; a palm resting over a lantern that then pinches simply grabs it (the lantern is within 13 cm of the pinch point). A grasp (curl > 0.75) is not open, so a cupped hand still grabs via the existing grasp rule rather than shading. Leave: one hand, palm down, over the water; the leave pose needs two palms facing each other. Fireflies: a hand held still over a lantern is openStill after 1 s and may get a firefly on it; that is a pleasant overlap, not a conflict, and the 7 cm window means a firefly-pose hand held at chest height (30-40 cm above the water, versus a lantern top 23 cm above it) is not shading. The open-hand attraction pulls the lantern toward the pinch point, which is exactly what keeps it under the palm; the nudge feature never pushes from joints above the top rim, so a palm on top does not shove it away. The wish-tracing feature uses a hand beside a held lantern, not above it.
harnessStep: Add cover, lit, bright, flame to world().lanterns entries and 'lanternsnuff', 'lanternflare' to the main.js event list. Step: L = nearest floating lantern (world coords); the palm joint (middle-finger-metacarpal) sits at wrist + (-0.009, 0.002, -0.031) for the right hand, so pose the right hand open (curl 0.05, pinch 0, pitchDeg 0, rollDeg 0, palm normal (0,-1,0)) at wrist [L.x + 0.009, L.y + 0.13 + 0.04, L.z + 0.031] (palm 4 cm over the top rim, fingers flat forward). frames(40): assert world().lanterns[L.i].cover > 0.8 and bright < 0.3 and the lantern's horizontal drift < 0.04 m (sheltered). Raise the wrist 0.3 m; frames(40): assert 'lanternflare' in events() and bright > 0.45 within those frames. Lower it back to the same pose and hold 140 frames (3.9 s at 1/36): assert 'lanternsnuff' in events() with detail.hand === 'right', world().lanterns[L.i].lit === false and flame < 0.05. Throughout: stats().hands.pinchR === false, no 'grab'/'pinchmiss', world().rig unchanged. Fireflies may land on the covering hand during the hold; the step does not depend on it.
risks: Accidental snuffing: a lantern attracted under a low, still open hand could be shaded without intent; mitigated by the 7 cm vertical window, the palm-down requirement and 3.5 s of steady cover, and nothing is ever lost (relight from another, or auto-rekindle without the flame feature). Quest palm-normal noise near the -0.6 threshold makes cover flicker: the 0.5 s ease and the decaying coverFor absorb it. On a held lantern (other hand) the top follows the pendulum and can slip out of the 9 cm window; acceptable, shading a floating one is the main case. The crackle muffling is applied at 0.5 s granularity, which is audible only as a small delay.

name: A wish on the paper
pitch: While one hand holds a lantern, the other index fingertip drawn slowly across its paper leaves a dark amber stroke, lit from inside like ink on a lantern shade, with a faint brush sound following the finger. The marks stay: release the lantern and your wish rises with it into the sky and becomes a star.
gesture: Per held lantern L (L.state === 'held', held by hand A = L.held) and the other hand B !== A with B.visible && B.active && !B.pinch.active && !B.grabbed && !B.submerged && B.joints['index-finger-tip'].valid; skip unless tip.distanceToSquared(L.position) < 0.2*0.2. Transform the tip into the body frame: tmp.inv.copy(tmp.m).invert() with the instance matrix composed this frame (rotation about L.top by yaw and lean, so the marks stay put as the lantern turns), local (x, y, z) with y in [-H, 0]. Profile radius R(y) by linear interpolation over the 8 lathe profile points ([0.046,0],[0.062,0.022],[0.071,0.06],[0.075,0.115],[0.073,0.17],[0.066,0.215],[0.054,0.245],[0.045,0.26], heights from the bottom, y + H); r = hypot(x, z); on the paper if |r - R(y)| < 0.018 && -H + 0.03 < y < -0.03 (the rings are excluded). Stroke start requires tip speed (B.joints['index-finger-tip'].velocity.length()) < 0.6 m/s so a slap does not write; a stroke continues while on the paper. UV from the LatheGeometry convention (x = R sin phi, z = R cos phi, u = phi/2pi, v = j/7): u = (atan2(x, z)/(2*PI) + 1) % 1, v = (j + frac)/7 for the profile segment j containing y. Paint into the lantern's 64x64 cell (cell = L.i, 6 columns x 4 rows) of a 384x256 R8 DataTexture: a 5x5 gaussian dot (peak alpha 0.6, additive, clamped 255) at (u*64, v*64), interpolated from the previous contact (u, v) of this hand in <= 8 steps with u wrapping; texture.needsUpdate = true only on frames that painted. L.ink = painted texels/4096 maintained incrementally (count a texel the first time it exceeds 40). Per-hand stroke state on the record: L.inkOn[hi], L.inkU[hi], L.inkV[hi]. ctx.lanterns.brush[hi] = { on, speed, pos: Vector3 } (allocated once) updated every frame for the audio follower. Emit 'lanternink' { pos: tip.clone(), hand: B, lantern: L } at each stroke start (rate-limited 0.2 s per lantern); ctx.lanterns.inked++ the first time a lantern gets a texel; L.heldFor accumulates while held (for the hint). respawnFar clears the cell (fill(0) on its 64 rows) and L.ink = 0.
visual: Bodies: new instanced attribute aIndex (Float32Array(MAX), set at spawn) -> varying vCell; new uniform uInk (the DataTexture, THREE.RedFormat, UnsignedByteType, LinearFilter, no mipmaps, 98 KB). conflicts: The tracing hand is open-ish with the index extended and never pinches; if it does pinch, the held lantern is skipped by handleGrabs (g.held) and the pinch becomes an ordinary miss/pull exactly as today, so no new meaning is given to pinch. A grasp of the tracing hand near a held lantern cannot grab it (graspNear excludes held grabbables). Held lanterns are never pushed by the nudge feature, so the finger does not swing the canvas. Leave: two hands, but the tracing hand is beside a lantern hanging below the other hand's pinch point, palms are not facing each other within 9 cm, and the holding hand is pinching (the leave detector requires no pinch). Fireflies: neither hand is still while tracing (the tracing hand moves at 0.05-0.3 m/s), and the holding hand is pinching, so no landing sequence starts. Water: the tracing hand is above the surface (submerged hands are excluded).
harnessStep: Add ink to world().lanterns entries and 'lanternink' to the main.js event list. Step: after 'lantern-grabbed' (right hand, pinch 1), lift 0.35 m over 24 frames and hold 40 frames so the string settles; read C = window.__nocturneCtx.lanterns.list[i].position. Target tip T = [C.x - 0.075, C.y - 0.02, C.z] (the widest ring, -X side). Marks on the far side are hidden from the player until the lantern turns; the held lantern spins slowly (0.4x) so that is fine. A full DataTexture re-upload (98 KB) per painted frame is trivial; it must not be flagged on idle frames. The held lantern sways when the holding hand moves; the tracing hand should be kept slow, and the harness keeps the holding hand still. Desktop mode has one hand, so this feature is XR-only.
angle: Lanterns as bodies with a flame. Every new act builds on the two things a lantern already does (it is pinched and carried on a string; it drifts toward an open hand) and on the per-instance bright/flame values the shaders, the water lights and the crackle already read, so none of it touches pinch or the two-hand vocabulary. In order of physical directness: an open hand can touch and nudge a floating lantern; a lit lantern held in the hand can pass its flame to a dark one (some arrivals now come dark, and a dark lantern has no lift); a palm laid over the top shades the flame, dims it, and held long enough puts it out; and while one hand holds a lantern the other index fingertip can trace a wish into its paper, which rises with it. Each adds zero draw calls (instance attributes, one small DataTexture) and only touches lanterns within arm's reach per frame.

name: Cupped light
pitch: Hold both hands together palm-up like a bowl and wait: fireflies drift over one by one and settle into the hollow of your hands until you are holding a small green lantern that lights your palms from inside. Lower the bowl to the surface and the light pours out into the lake — each firefly touches the water, leaves a plankton ring, and drifts away dim.
gesture: Both hands a,b = ctx.hands.list. FORM when for both: visible && active && !submerged && !pinch.active && !grabbed && !grasp && meanCurl < 0.55; palm.normal.y > 0.55 (palms up); d = a.palm.position.distanceTo(b.palm.position) in [0.08, 0.26]; a.stillFor > 0.6 && b.stillFor > 0.6. Once formed it HOLDS with relaxed hysteresis so the player can move to pour: both visible, !pinch.active, !grasp, meanCurl < 0.65, palm.normal.y > 0.25, d < 0.32, palm.speed <= 0.45 each, with a 0.5 s grace if one hand drops tracking (same trick as leave.js). Cup point C = midpoint of the two palm.position + normalize(a.palm.normal + b.palm.normal) * 0.05; radius r = clamp(0.35*d, 0.04, 0.09). While cupped, hf.attract is forced false for both hands (no fingertip landings on the bowl). POUR when cupped && cup.count >= 1 && C.y < ctx.water.level + 0.08 (fires while the wrists are still ~1.5 cm above the surface; submersion would break the hold). FREE (spill) when the hold conditions fail (hands opened apart, a pinch, a fast move, tracking lost > 0.5 s).
visual: Zero new draw calls: two new per-firefly states CUP(4) and POUR(5) in the existing typed arrays / Points + mirror. Recruit: while formed, every 0.4 + 0.3*rnd s the nearest WANDER firefly with cooldown <= 0 within 14 m becomes CUP, up to CUP_MAX = round(20 * particleScale). CUP steering: target = C + r*(cos(al)*sin(be), cos(be), sin(al)*sin(be)) with al = seed*6.28 + t*0.6 (slow orbit), be = 0.4 + seed*2.3; speed min(0.6, 0.08 + 2.2*dist), velocity ease k = min(1, dt*3.5) (the APPROACH easing); brightness inbound max(blink, 0.35), settled (dist < 0.05) 0.85 + 0.15*sin(t*3 + seed*20). Hand glow with no draw calls: add st.glow = { position: Vector3, amount: 0 } to HandState in hands.js makeState and let updateVisuals drive uWarmOn toward max(grabbed ? 1 : 0, st.glow.amount) and set uWarm / uWarmColor from st.glow (CONFIG.colors.firefly) when nothing is grabbed — the existing 1/(1+45 d^2) warm term lights the cupped palms from inside; fireflies set glow.amount = min(1, cup.count/8) at C every frame (0 when not cupped). POUR: each CUP firefly sinks at vy = -0.25 m/s (this state bypasses the yMin clamp) to level + 0.02 where it touches: ctx.water.disturb(x, z, 0.06, 0.12) (at most 4 touches per frame, staggered by seed to stay inside the 16-slot budget), brightness spikes to 1 then falls to 0 over 0.6 s, then WANDER with cooldown 8 s and brightness ramping back over 3 s as it drifts home; one larger ring at pour start: disturb(C.x, C.z, 0.25, 0.35) (the lotus bloom is 0.18/0.28). Energy +0.015 per poured firefly, capped at +0.3 per pour.
sound: 'fireflycup' { pos: C.clone(), count } emitted when count reaches 1, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 → sfx: glass bell midi pitchFor(step, 6) (the six steps walk up the pentatonic as the bowl fills), gain 0.12, dur 1.4, wet 0.4. Continuous: a per-hand 'hand voice' (2 sines at the chord root and fifth +36 semitones with 0.2 Hz ±8 ct vibrato → lowpass 3 kHz → gain → api.spatial refDistance 0.8; 4 persistent nodes per hand, shared by the other firefly proposals) updated in sfx.update's existing 30 Hz control block from ctx.fireflies.cup = { count, position }: gain target 0.05 * smoothstep(0, 12, count) via setTargetAtTime tau 0.4, panner at C. 'fireflypour' { pos, count } → sfx: four descending glass bells pitchFor(6,5,4,3; register 6) 90 ms apart, gain 0.14, wet 0.6, plus noiseBurst at C (dur 0.25, bandpass 900 → 300, gain 0.1: a hush of water); music: ctx.music.requestSwell('pad_bioluminescence', 0.3); ambience: S.startle(3, 5) (the crickets pause as the lake lights up). 'fireflyfree' { pos, count } → two quick tings (pickTuned TINGS) gain 0.06.

name: The ribbon
pitch: Carry an open hand slowly through the dark, palm up, and fireflies peel off the nearest cloud and string out behind it — a soft ribbon of light 3–4 m long that follows every slow curve of your hand. Stop, and the ribbon gathers and lands on your fingers; move fast and it scatters.
gesture: Per hand h: visible && active && !submerged && !pinch.active && !grabbed && open (every curl < 0.35) && palm.normal.y > 0.15 (palm up-ish) && !still (stillDisp >= 0.03) && palm.speed in [0.05, 0.35] && palm.speedH >= 0.6 * palm.speed (a sideways drift, not a vertical stroke) → 'drifting'. Accumulate drifting time into slowFor; a dip below 0.05 m/s is tolerated for 0.4 s (a pause), palm.speed > 0.5 or any other failure resets slowFor to 0. Recruit while slowFor > 0.5 s. A hand that becomes openStill keeps its followers and hands them to the landing slots; pinch, submersion, a closed hand, or tracking loss > 0.4 s releases them (WANDER, cooldown 4 s).
visual: Zero new draw calls: new state FOLLOW(6) with followHand/followIdx Int8Arrays. Recruit every 0.3 s the nearest WANDER firefly (cooldown <= 0) within 14 m, up to FOLLOW_MAX = round(16 * particleScale) per hand. Per hand a trail ring: Float32Array(3*256) of T = palm.position + palm.normal * 0.09, sampled at 24 Hz (accumulate dt; 10.6 s of history) with a head index. Follower k targets sample (head - round((k+1) * 0.22 * 24)) mod 256 plus a seeded ±0.03 m offset, so the strand trails the hand as a ribbon about 3.5 s long; inbound followers (> 0.3 m from their target) head for the live T at <= 0.6 m/s; steering is the APPROACH easing (sp = min(0.6, 0.08 + 2.2 d), k = min(1, dt*3.5)). Brightness: inbound max(blink, 0.35); on the ribbon 0.7 + 0.2*sin(t*2.1 + seed*31) (steady, so it reads as a line of light). Hand-off: when the hand becomes openStill, each free SLOT_JOINTS slot takes the nearest follower as APPROACH (instant landings); the rest hover on the last samples. The existing repel (speed > 0.7 within 0.6 m) scatters them. ctx.fireflies gains followers[2], followArrived[2], followCentroid (Float32Array(6), accumulated in the main loop, no allocation).

Continuous: the per-hand 'hand voice' (sine + triangle at chord root and fifth +24 semitones, 0.25 Hz ±6 ct vibrato → bandpass Q 4 → gain → api.spatial refDistance 1) placed each frame at ctx.fireflies.followCentroid for that hand; in the 30 Hz control block gain target 0.035 * smoothstep(0, 10, followArrived[hi]) via setTargetAtTime tau 0.3.
discoverability: It sits on the gradient the player already knows (still → they land, fast → they scatter): the first time someone drifts an open hand slowly through the dark a few lights peel off and trail after it, and the bell on the first arrival confirms it. Hint id 'ribbon', text 'move an open hand slowly and they follow', after 130 s, ready: s.touchedWater, done: s.followed (first 'fireflyfollow').

Leave needs two still hands with palms facing each other (normal.y ≈ 0): excluded by palm.normal.y > 0.15 and by !still. Landing requires still and this requires !still — adjacent bands, joined by the hand-off, so the two read as one behaviour. The vertical-beat gesture of 'The far ones answer' is excluded by speedH >= 0.6 * speed.

name: Carried light
pitch: Close your hand around the fireflies resting on it and they stay, a heartbeat of green light showing through your glass fingers. Lift the closed hand to eye level and open it to the sky: they rise together in a slow fountain, and the one you carried longest becomes a new star.
gesture: Prerequisite: >= 1 LANDED firefly on hand h. Landed fireflies now leave when h.palm.speed > 0.35 (today: h.speed, the max joint speed) so curling fingers no longer spooks them — they ride the joints in (they are already placed at joint.position + palm.normal*0.01). CATCH the frame h.meanCurl rises past 0.6 while visible && !submerged && !pinch.active && !grabbed → every LANDED firefly on h becomes CAUGHT (state 7), its slot released. HOLD while meanCurl > 0.45 && visible && !submerged && !pinch.active (a whole-hand grasp that grabs a lantern at meanCurl > 0.75 sets pinch.active, which spills them). OPEN when meanCurl < 0.35: if palm.normal.y > 0.5 && palm.position.y > playerCtl.state.headWorld.y - 0.15 (offered to the sky at eye level or above) → RISE; otherwise a gentle spill (burst strength 0.7, cooldown 5).
visual: Zero new draw calls. CAUGHT: position = palm.position + palm.normal*0.025 + seeded ±0.015 (inside the fist), brightness 0.5 + 0.4*(0.5 + 0.5*sin(t*7.5 + seed*13)) — a 1.2 Hz heartbeat seen through the translucent hand; the hand glows through the same st.glow hook as Cupped light (amount = min(1, 0.4 + 0.15*count), position = fist point, firefly colour). RISE (state 8, bypasses the yMax band clamp): vy = 0.35 + 0.25*rnd, lateral wander 0.05*sin(t*1.3 + seed*9), brightness 1.0 for 5 s then fading to 0 over 2 s; at 7 s the lowest-index firefly of the group becomes a star via ctx.sky.addLanternStar(dir = (pos - headWorld).normalize()) → 'fireflystar' { dir, pos, count } (sky.js emits 'starborn' as it does for lanterns); all of the group are moved, while dark, back to their home cloud and resume WANDER (cooldown 6, brightness ramping back over 3 s). Energy +0.08 on RISE (a lotus is 0.15).

'fireflyrise' { pos, count } → noiseBurst kind 'pink', bandpass 800 → 2400 sweep, dur 0.5, gain 0.06 (a breath of air). 'fireflystar' { dir, pos, count } → sfx: two ascending glass bells pitchFor(d0, 7) and pitchFor(d0+1, 7) 110 ms apart, gain 0.08, wet 0.8, refDistance 25 at head + dir*30, plus the pure sine on the chord's fifth (index 0) gain 0.1 — the lantern-star sparkle at half size, and no pad swell, so it stays intimate.

Hint id 'catch', text 'close your hand on them, then open it to the sky', after 160 s, ready: s.fireflyLanded, done: s.caught (first 'fireflycatch').

name: The far ones answer
pitch: Raise and lower an open palm-up hand slowly, like breathing, and the nearest cloud of fireflies out on the lake begins to flash on your beat — by the third stroke the whole cloud blinks together each time your hand reaches the bottom, and a bell sounds from out there with it. Stop, and over half a minute they drift back into their own rhythm.
gesture: One hand h: visible && active && !submerged && !pinch.active && !grabbed && open (every curl < 0.35) && palm.normal.y > 0.3. Beat detector on rig-local palm motion: yv = h.palm.velocityLocal.y; track yMax of h.palm.filtered.y since the last beat; a BEAT is the frame yv crosses from < -0.08 to > +0.03 (the bottom of a downstroke) with yMax - filtered.y >= 0.05 m and, from the second beat on, 0.7 s <= interval <= 3.5 s. period = the interval at beat 2, then an EMA with alpha 0.5. A run ends when no beat arrives within 2*period + 0.5 s, or the base conditions fail. Vertical by construction: a 6 cm stroke at 2 s peaks at ~0.19 m/s, under the 0.35 m/s that would lift landed fireflies, and the ribbon gesture's speedH >= 0.6*speed test keeps the two apart.
visual: Zero new draw calls: it works on the existing flash phases. Target cloud k = the home nearest the palm (ctx.fireflies.homes; usually the 3.6 m front-left cloud). On each beat, for every non-steady WANDER/SCATTER firefly of cloud k: period[i] = lerp(period[i], clamp(beatPeriod, 1.0, 3.4), 0.5) and phase[i] blended toward the value that makes its flash peak on the predicted next beat: target = (rise_i - (t + beatPeriod)) mod pd_i (rise_i = FLASH.rise*(0.85 + 0.3*seed), as blink() uses), coupling 0.6 on beat 1, 0.75 on beat 2, 0.85 from beat 3, plus ±0.06 s seeded jitter so it stays alive; during a run the cloud's Kuramoto gain kg[k] is pinned at SYNC.kMax*SYNC.dt so the existing mean-field pass holds them on the beat between strokes. lock is computed in the existing 0.25 s sync pass with the same accumulators: |mean exp(i(theta_i - 2*pi*rise_i/pd_i - theta_beat))|, theta_beat = 2*pi*(t - tLastBeat)/period → ctx.fireflies.conduct = { hand, beats, period, cloud, lock }. A locked beat (lock > 0.5) lifts that cloud's flash peak by (1 + 0.25*lock) for one cycle and adds energy +0.015 (cap 1), so a long conducting run slowly brightens the aurora. Run end: period[i] = period0[i] (a copy kept from init) and the natural swell-and-relax takes over — the cloud drifts out of your rhythm over ~30 s.
sound: 'fireflybeat' { pos: the cloud centre as {x,y,z} (not a scratch vector), hand, period, lock, n } on every beat → sfx: only when lock >= 0.35 (silence while it is still gathering): a glass bell at the cloud centre, midi pitchFor(n % 5, 5), gain 0.08 + 0.14*lock, dur 1.1*period, wet 0.5, refDistance 3 — the cloud sings as it flashes, which also localises it. music: when lock >= 0.7 on four consecutive beats, once per run, ctx.music.requestSwell('pad_northern_swell', 0.25). Add 'period' and 'lock' to summarize()'s kept keys in main.js so the event log carries them.
discoverability: The clouds already breathe into and out of synchrony on their own, and a slow rise-and-fall of an open hand is what people do at distant lights; two strokes are enough to see the cloud's flashes pull toward the hand's rhythm, and the bell from the cloud confirms it. Hint id 'conduct', text 'raise and lower an open hand, slowly', after 240 s, ready: s.fireflyLanded && nearest home within 9 m of headWorld, done: s.conducted (a 'fireflybeat' with lock >= 0.5).
conflicts: No pinch (pinch.active aborts the run), so pinch-pull locomotion and grabs are untouched. Leave needs still hands with palms facing each other — excluded by palm.normal.y > 0.3 and by the required motion. Landing needs still; a beating hand is not still, but landed fireflies stay because palm.speed stays under 0.35 (an accidental beat while fireflies rest on the hand simply makes the far cloud answer). The ribbon needs horizontal drift; this needs vertical strokes.
harnessStep: Right hand open, palm up: for f = 0..399: setHand('right', [0.25, 1.25 + 0.06*Math.sin(2*Math.PI*f/72), -0.45], 0, { pitchDeg: 0, rollDeg: 180, curl: 0.02 }); await frame() — a 2 s breath, 12 cm peak-to-peak, peak speed 0.19 m/s (beats at frames ≈ 54, 126, 198, 270, 342). Then step('firefly-conduct', events().filter(e => e.type === 'fireflybeat').length >= 4 && ctx.fireflies.conduct.lock >= 0.6 && Math.abs(ctx.fireflies.conduct.period - 2.0) < 0.2 && ctx.fireflies.conduct.cloud === 0, { lock, period, beats }), and assert stats().fireflyLanded did not grow during the sweep (it is not a landing pose).
risks: Beat detection on jittery real hands is the main risk; the 5 cm amplitude, 0.7 s minimum interval and the 120 ms filtered palm position are the guards, but it needs one tuning pass on device. The payoff lives 3.6–7 m away and can be missed if the player faces elsewhere; the bell at the cloud centre and choosing the nearest cloud mitigate it. Retiming ~100 fireflies per beat is O(cloud) and allocation-free; the sync pass is unchanged in cost.
angle: Deepen the fireflies by turning the one rule the player already knows (still open hand → they land; fast hand → they scatter) into a spectrum of slow gestures — cup, drift, close, breathe — each read straight from the real HandState fields, each answered by the existing 300-point cloud with zero new draw calls, using the hand material's existing warm-glow uniforms and the wave sim's plankton light as the only new "renderers".

name: Lantern among the lily pads
pitch: Carry a lantern over to a closed lotus cluster and let it go in the water: the pads hold it there, its amber light falls on the petals, and after a few seconds the bud opens slowly, as if warmed. A lantern left among the pads keeps that flower open for as long as it stays.
gesture: No new gesture. Existing grab (h.pinch.justStarted with L.grab within CONFIG.hands.grabRadius 0.13 + 0.12 of h.pinch.point) and existing in-water release (h.pinch.justReleased while L.top.y - 0.26 <= ctx.water.level, which already floats it with 'lanternsplash'). New lantern-side condition evaluated in lotus.update over ctx.lanterns.list (6 flowers x <=24 lanterns, hypot only): L.state === 'floating' && L.touched (new flag set in onGrab, so only lanterns the player has handled count, never ones that drift by on their own) && !L.incoming && L.bright > 0.3 && hypot(L.position.x - f.position.x, L.position.z - f.position.z) < 0.45 (enter) / > 0.55 (exit, hysteresis). Per flower f.warm += dt while near, -= 2*dt otherwise, clamped 0..3.5. When f.warm > 2.5 && f.bloom < 0.25 && !f.open -> openFlower(i, 'lantern') with f.openSeconds = 5.0 (touch keeps 1.6), energy +0.08, disturb(0.18, 0.18). While near && f.state === 'open': f.timer = min(f.timer, f.stay - 10) so it closes only 10 s after the lantern leaves. Fingertip touch (any h.visible tips[k] within 0.08 of f.bud) still works independently. In lanterns.js floating branch: if nearest ctx.lotus.clusters entry is within 0.40 m horizontally, damp wind+walk+homing (vx,vz *= 0.25) before the hand-attraction and separation terms are added, and set L.amongPads = true; an open hand within ATTRACT_RADIUS can still coax it out.
visual: Zero new draw calls. lotus flower InstancedMesh gets a dynamic InstancedBufferAttribute aLantern (vec4, 6 instances: xyz of the brightest lantern within 0.6 m of that flower, w = L.bright * smoothstep(0.6, 0.35, distance), else 0). LOTUS_FLOWER_VERT, next to the existing uMoonDir Lambert, adds vWarm = aLantern.w * max(dot(worldNormal, normalize(aLantern.xyz - worldPos)), 0) / (1 + 12*d2); LOTUS_FLOWER_FRAG adds vWarm * vec3(1.0, 0.70, 0.34) * 0.9 (CONFIG.colors.lantern). Glow halo gain (existing S.glowGain per frame) gets + 0.10 * smoothstep(f.warm, 0, 1); the mirror quad follows automatically. The slow 5 s open is the existing easeOutCubic path with a per-flower f.openSeconds instead of the OPEN_SECONDS constant. Petals therefore read amber on the lantern side and pale on the moon side.
sound: 'lotusbloom' gains a `cause` field ('touch' | 'lantern'); sfx onLotus: when e.cause === 'lantern' -> triggerBell({ midi: pitchFor(e.note, 5), pos: e.pos, gain: 0.32, dur: 5.0, kind: 'ceramic', attack: 0.35, wet: 0.4, tag: 'lotus' }) so the note swells instead of striking, tuned bowl layer gain 0.18 (was 0.25). The lantern's own crackle keeps running on the nearest-3 slots, and the existing 'lanternsplash' sample plays at set-down. No music/ambience change (a chain of six lantern-lit flowers still reaches the existing 'lotuschord' swell + cricket hush).
discoverability: Both halves are already taught by the 'lantern' and 'lotus' hints; the near lantern (front-right, 0.55 m) and cluster 0 (front-left, 0.65 m) are an arm's length apart, so setting a lantern down next to the flower is the natural first experiment. New hint pushed into HINTS: { id: 'lanternlotus', text: 'leave a lantern among the lily pads', after: 130, done: (ctx, s) => s.lanternBloomed, ready: (ctx, s) => s.grabbed && s.bloomed && nearestLotus(ctx) < REACH + 0.15 && nearestLantern(ctx) < REACH + 0.15 }; s.lanternBloomed set from 'lotusbloom' with e.cause === 'lantern'.
conflicts: Pinch semantics untouched: the only pinches involved are the existing lantern grab and its release. Setting down = release below the surface, already an existing path. No two-hand pose, nothing near the leave gesture. Firefly landing untouched (hand may even be open-still while the lantern warms the bud). L.touched guard prevents lanterns that home toward the player (they stop at 0.7 m, right beside cluster 0) from opening buds spontaneously. Lantern-lit flowers still count for 'lotuschord' via the existing chordArmed once-per-episode guard.
harnessStep: After the existing 'lotus-bloomed' step (which opens cluster 0 by touch), pick B = nearest flower with !open from world().lotus (cluster 5 at az ~ -64 deg, 1.4-3.8 m, may be out of reach; so instead run this step BEFORE the touch step using B = cluster 0 and L2 = nearest floating lantern from world().lanterns, both < 0.8 m from head). setHand('right', [L2.x, L2.y + 0.12, L2.z], 0); frames(12); setHand(..., 1); frames(12); assert events() has 'grab'. Carry over 48 frames along a lerp to [B.x + 0.30, level + 0.10, B.z] (pinch 1) - the pinch point stays 0.30 m from the bud so tips (< 0.2 m from the pinch point) never come within TOUCH_RADIUS 0.08; the lantern's bottom hangs 0.34 m below the pinch point so it is under water. setHand(..., 0) at the same spot; frames(6); assert 'lanternsplash' in events(). Park the hand at [0.25, 1.25, -0.4]; frames(144) (4 s at 1/36 s). Assert: events().some(e => e.type === 'lotusbloom' && e.detail.cause === 'lantern' && e.detail.index === B.index) (add 'cause' to the summarize() key list), world().lotus[B.index].open === true and bloom < 1 (still opening, proves the 5 s path), world().lanterns[L2.index].pads === true (add `pads: !!l.amongPads` to world()), and window.__nocturneCtx.lotus.flowers[B.index].warm > 2.5. step('lantern-warms-lotus', ok, {...}). Then set clock.step = 0.1 for 700 frames (70 s > STAY_MAX 75 minus margin; use 800) and assert the flower is still open (the lantern keeps it awake) - optional second assertion.
risks: The pendulum is buoyant, so a lantern lowered into the water bobs; the enter/exit hysteresis (0.45/0.55) and the 2.5 s dwell absorb that, but the numbers need a look on a real headset. The shader edit must keep the fragment's tone-mapping/colour-space chunks intact. A player who parks lanterns on all six clusters can hold the chord open indefinitely - acceptable, it is only glow and pads, but note that the music swell fires once per episode. name: Firefly escort
pitch: Let a lantern go while fireflies are resting on that hand (or any fireflies are nearby) and they lift off with it, spiralling around the flame as it rises, its light flaring with them. A few metres up the lantern outpaces them and they spill away in a shower of sparks, and the cloud they came from flashes in step for a while, as if passing the news along.
gesture: No new gesture. Chain of existing conditions: fireflies land on a hand via h.openStill (open && stillFor > 1.0 && !submerged); they stay LANDED as long as hf.hold (h.visible && !h.submerged && h.speed <= 0.35), which does not require the hand to be open, so a hand that closes a pinch slowly (index/thumb tips moving < 0.35 m/s; h.pinch.active after distance < 0.020 for 2 frames) keeps its fireflies and grabs a lantern within 0.25 m of h.pinch.point. Lift at any speed (fireflies leave the hand above 0.35 m/s, but are still within recruit range); h.pinch.justReleased with L.top.y - 0.26 > level -> 'lanternrelease'. On that event fireflies.js recruits up to 10: any WANDER firefly (cooldown <= 0) within 3.0 m of e.lantern.position, plus any LANDED/APPROACH firefly within 0.6 m of it (i.e. on the releasing hand); nearest-first via a fixed Int16Array(10)/Float32Array(10) insertion, no allocation. Recruited -> state ESCORT (4), escortL[i] = L.i, releaseSlot(i). Spill when L.state !== 'rising' (caught again, or became a star) || L.riseTime > 4.2 (riseSpeed passes ~1 m/s there): one-shot per lantern.
visual: Zero new draw calls (same Points + mirror). ESCORT steering per frame: a = t*2.6 + seed[i]*6.283, r = 0.14 + 0.12*seed[i]; target = (L.position.x + cos(a)*r, L.position.y + 0.05 + (seed[i]-0.5)*0.25, L.position.z + sin(a)*r); desired speed min(1.0, 0.15 + d*3), velocity lerp k = min(1, dt*5), bright = max(blink(i), 0.55). fireflies.js writes L.escorts = n on the lantern record each frame (zeroed first for rising lanterns); lanterns.js rising branch reads it: L.flame target 1 + 0.3*min(1, (L.escorts||0)/4), i.e. the flame quad grows a third while escorted. Spill: vel = outward*0.9 + (rnd-0.5)*0.3, vy = -0.25 + rnd*0.3, state SCATTER, timer = t + 1.0 + rnd*0.6, cooldown 4, bright 1 -> the existing SCATTER damping and yMin clamp let them drift down and out. Home-cloud answer: at spill set S.syncKick[k] = 6 s for the cloud most escorts came from; the existing Kuramoto pass uses kg[k] = max(kg[k], 1.5*SYNC.kMax*R*SYNC.dt) while syncKick > 0, so ctx.fireflies.coherence[k] climbs toward 1 over a few seconds and that cloud flashes together.
sound: Two new events, both logged: 'fireflyescort' { pos: L.position.clone(), count, lantern } at recruit and 'fireflyspill' { pos, count, lantern } at spill. sfx: 'fireflyescort' -> ascending sparkle, for k < min(count, 5): triggerBell({ midi: pitchFor(k, 6), pos, gain: 0.07, dur: 0.9, kind: 'glass', when: now + 0.05 + k*0.09, wet: 0.5, tag: 'escort' }); 'fireflyspill' -> four descending tings pitchFor(4 - k, 6) 70 ms apart gain 0.05 plus noiseBurst({ type: 'highpass', freq: 4000, q: 0.7, dur: 0.3, gain: 0.03 }) as a wing flutter. The existing 'lanternrelease' whoosh, low ceramic bell and pad swell already underlie it; no music/ambience change.
discoverability: Every lantern released within 3 m of a firefly cloud gets a few escorts (the back-left starter lantern is ~1.9 m from the fringe of cloud 0), so the first release most players make already shows it; the full version (a hand-full of fireflies riding up) is discovered by anyone who does the two taught things in sequence. Optional hint: { id: 'escort', text: 'let a lantern go with fireflies on your hand', after: 200, done: (ctx, s) => s.escorted, ready: (ctx, s) => s.fireflyLanded && s.released && nearestLantern(ctx) < REACH + 0.15 } with s.released from 'lanternrelease' and s.escorted from 'fireflyescort' (count >= 3).
conflicts: Triggered by the existing 'lanternrelease' only; the pinch/grab/locomotion code is not touched. The 3 s re-grab window still works: L.state becomes 'held' and escorts spill immediately. Fireflies in ESCORT are not WANDER so hands cannot recruit them, and the fast-hand repel loop scatters them like any other (releaseSlot + burst, escortL cleared). Nothing two-handed. Landing behaviour unchanged - the feature only reads slotHand at release time.
harnessStep: Right after the existing 'firefly-landed' step (200 frames palm-up, fireflyLanded > 0): let L2 = nearest floating lantern from world(). Move the right hand slowly (keeps h.speed < 0.35): 72 frames lerping the palm-up pose { pitchDeg: 0, rollDeg: 180 } from [0.3, 1.3, -0.45] to [L2.x, L2.y + 0.15, L2.z + 0.10] (wrist; fingers extend -Z so the tips sit over the lantern, pinch point within 0.25 m of its centre). Ramp pinch 0 -> 1 over 24 frames (tip travel ~5 cm at ~0.08 m/s, below the 0.35 leave speed); assert 'grab' in events() and window.__nocturneCtx.fireflies.landedCount > 0 still. Lift 0.40 m over 54 frames (0.27 m/s) with pinch 1, then pinch 0 at the top; frames(4). Assert events().some(e => e.type === 'fireflyescort' && e.detail.count >= 1) and stats().fireflyEscorting >= 1 (add `fireflyEscorting: ctx.fireflies.escortCount` to stats()). Park the hand; frames(180) (5 s). Assert 'fireflyspill' present, stats().fireflyEscorting === 0, and max over the next 8 s (step 0.1, 80 frames) of window.__nocturneCtx.fireflies.coherence[k] > 0.7 for the kicked cloud (expose ctx.fireflies.kickedCloud). Fallback proof if the landed fireflies leave during the pinch: the 3 m radius still recruits from cloud 0's fringe (seeded PRNG makes the count deterministic), so count >= 1 holds either way.
risks: 1.0 m/s is faster than anything else fireflies do; keep the escort to <= 4.2 s and cap it at 10 fireflies so it reads as a rush of light, not a swarm. L.escorts on the lantern record is a cross-module field (document in both headers); module order lanterns -> fireflies means the flame flare lags one frame (fine). State number 4 must not collide with the pollen chain's VISIT/CARRY if both are built. The timejump handler must clamp nothing for ESCORT (it keys on L.riseTime), but SCATTER timers set at spill are already clamped.
