name: Pollen chain
pitch: Touch a bud and its bloom calls fireflies: three or four fly in from the nearest cloud, hover in a slow loop above the open flower and take on its colour. When they leave, one of them may carry that colour to the next closed bud and open it, so a single touch can wander from cluster to cluster around the lake; and a coloured firefly that later lands on your hand sings that flower's note instead of a random one.
gesture: No new gesture. Start: the existing touch (any h.visible hand's h.tips[k].distanceToSquared(f.bud) < 0.08^2 while f.bloom < 0.25 && !f.open) or a lantern-warmed bloom; everything after is firefly behaviour. On 'lotusbloom' (any cause) fireflies.js recruits up to 4 WANDER fireflies with cooldown <= 0 within 6.0 m of e.pos, nearest first (fixed small arrays, one O(N) scan per bloom, blooms are rate-limited by the flowers themselves) -> state VISIT (5), visitF[i] = e.index, timer[i] = t, stay[i] = 6 + rnd*6, tint rgb = flower colour, visitNote[i] = e.note, carrier[i] = 1 for the first recruit only. Leave when t - timer > stay || flowers[visitF].bloom < 0.5: if carrier && rnd() < ctx.fireflies.carryChance (0.5, exposed for tests) && global CARRY count < 2 && t - lastFireflyBloom > 6: pick nearest flower j with !open && bloom < 0.25 within 4.0 m of the current flower -> state CARRY (6), visitF = j; else existing burst() upward -> SCATTER -> WANDER with cooldown 5. CARRY: fly to flowers[j].bud + (0, 0.05, 0) at min(0.5, 0.08 + d*2.0); at d < 0.06 -> ctx.lotus.open(j, 'firefly') (payload cause 'firefly', energy +0.08, disturb(0.18, 0.18), f.openSeconds 3.0), then VISIT on j. Landing on a hand unchanged (existing openStill / hf.still path) but the 'fireflyland' payload adds note: tintMix > 0.3 ? visitNote[i] : -1.
visual: Zero new draw calls. Points geometry gets a dynamic BufferAttribute aTint (Float32Array N*4: rgb + mix), uploaded each frame like position/aBright. FIREFLY_VERT and FIREFLY_MIRROR_VERT pass varying vec4 vTint; FIREFLY_FRAG replaces its uColor use with mix(uColor, vTint.rgb, vTint.a * 0.85) before the existing amber-at-peak warming, so a visiting firefly turns pink/lilac/gold and fades back over 12 s (mix -= dt/12 in every non-VISIT/CARRY state, += dt/2 while hovering). VISIT motion: a = t*1.8 + seed*6.283; target = f.bud + (cos(a)*0.06, 0.07 + 0.02*sin(1.7a), sin(a)*0.06); speed min(0.55, 0.08 + d*2.2), k = dt*3.5; bright = 0.45 + 0.45*|sin(t*1.5 + seed*9)| (steady warm hover, not the Photinus flash). lotus.js reads ctx.fireflies.visitors (Uint8Array(6), zeroed and counted in the firefly loop each frame) and adds 0.08*min(3, visitors[i]) to the glow gain, so a visited flower brightens; the mirror quad follows. The 3 s firefly-caused bloom uses the per-flower openSeconds path.
sound: New logged event 'lotusvisit' { pos: bud.clone(), index, note, count } at recruit -> sfx: noiseBurst({ type: 'highpass', freq: 4500, q: 0.8, dur: 0.22, gain: 0.035, pos }) as a wing flutter plus two glass bells triggerBell({ midi: pitchFor(e.note, 6) }) and pitchFor(e.note + 2, 6) 130 ms apart, gain 0.06, dur 1.4, wet 0.6. 'lotusbloom' with cause 'firefly' in onLotus: gain 0.32, attack 0.12, bowl layer 0.18 (a lighter strike than a touch). 'fireflyland' with note >= 0: onFirefly uses pitchFor(e.note, 6) instead of the random D6-A6 degree, so a pollinated firefly lands on the flower's pitch (notePlayed feeds the aurora voice as before). A chain that reaches all six triggers the existing 'lotuschord' pad swell and cricket hush; no other music/ambience change.
discoverability: It happens on the very first bud the player opens: cluster 0 (az -55, 0.65 m) is about 3.0 m from cloud 0 (az -40, 3.6 m), inside the 6 m recruit range, so fireflies arrive within seconds of the taught 'the buds open when you touch them' moment, right in front of the player. No hint text needed; the carry to the next bud is the reward for watching (a bell sounds from the next cluster).
conflicts: Trigger is the existing 'lotusbloom'; nothing about pinch, grab, locomotion or the leave pose changes. VISIT/CARRY fireflies are not WANDER, so hand recruiting never steals a visitor; the fast-hand repel and every releaseSlot path also clear visitF/carrier so a scattered visitor drops its errand. Landing on hands keeps the same conditions; only the payload note changes. A CARRY firefly opening a bud is gated to 1 bloom per 6 s and <= 2 carriers at once so a chain never reads as a cascade or a game.
harnessStep: After the existing 'lotus-bloomed' step: frames(216) (6 s at 1/36). Assert events().some(e => e.type === 'lotusvisit' && e.detail.count >= 1 && e.detail.index === B.index) and stats().fireflyVisiting >= 1 (add `fireflyVisiting: ctx.fireflies.visitingCount` to stats()); also window.__nocturneCtx.fireflies.tint has some entry with mix > 0.3 (read via page.evaluate over ctx.fireflies.tint). Then force the chain deterministically: page.evaluate(() => { window.__nocturneCtx.fireflies.carryChance = 1; window.__fakeXR.clock.step = 0.05; }); run 600 frames (30 s; hover 6-12 s + flight <= 4 m at 0.5 m/s). Assert events().some(e => e.type === 'lotusbloom' && e.detail.cause === 'firefly') ('cause' added to summarize()) and world().lotus.filter(f => f.open).length >= 2. Restore step 1/36. Optional: with hands parked at rest (open, still) a pollinated firefly may land; if a 'fireflyland' event has detail.note >= 0 assert it equals the visited flower's note.

The timejump handler must clamp VISIT timers like LANDED. Bells from a far cluster the player is not looking at could be puzzling the first time (mitigated by the flower's glow and the fireflies' visible flight). If Firefly escort is also built the enum values must be coordinated, and a firefly cannot be both an escort and a visitor (escort recruiting must skip VISIT/CARRY).

All four add zero draw calls (new dynamic attributes on existing InstancedMesh/Points), allocate nothing per frame (typed arrays; Vector3.clone() only inside rare event emits, matching the existing lotus/lantern pattern), and are O(N) at most once per event. If more than one is built, coordinate the new firefly state numbers (ESCORT=4, VISIT=5, CARRY=6) and the shared `cause` key added to main.js summarize().

name: The lake passes it on
pitch: When a released lantern finally becomes a star, the news travels back across the water: a wave of firefly flashes rolls outward from where you stand at walking pace, and every open lotus it passes brightens and restates its note. The crickets fall silent for a breath, then resume.
gesture: No new gesture; reward for patience. Existing chain only: grab (h.pinch.justStarted within 0.25 m of a lantern), release with h.pinch.justReleased while L.top.y - 0.26 > level -> rising -> 25 s later becomeStar() emits 'lanternstar'. fireflies.js and lotus.js subscribe to 'lanternstar' and store waveAt = t + 0.8 (so the star's own three-bell sparkle strikes first) and the wave origin ox, oz = ctx.playerCtl.state.headWorld. On the first update with t >= waveAt: fireflies does one O(N) pass over WANDER/SCATTER fireflies with steady[i] === 0: d = hypot(x - ox, z - oz); phase[i] = ((-(t + d / 2.5)) % period[i] + period[i]) % period[i], so each firefly's next Photinus flash peaks exactly as a 2.5 m/s front reaches it; S.waveHold = 6 suppresses the Kuramoto nudge (kg[k] = 0) so the clouds do not fight the wave; emits 'lakewave' { pos: head.clone(), count } once. lotus.js sets f.waveAt = t + 0.8 + hypot(f.position.x - ox, f.position.z - oz) / 2.5 for every open flower.
visual: Zero new draw calls and no shader change. Fireflies: the existing blink() envelope does the work, the pass only rewrites phase[], so cloud 0 (3.6 m) lights up ~1.4 s after the star and cloud 2 (7.2 m) ~2.9 s after: a visible band of light 1.5 m wide sweeping across the lake. Lotus: the global surge (S.surgeT) becomes per-flower: sf = sin(pi * clamp((t - f.waveAt) / 2.0, 0, 1)); the glow size/gain loop uses surgeF = max(surge, 0.7 * sf) for that instance (two lines) and uSurge stays max over flowers so the petal shimmer answers too. Lanterns unchanged.
sound: 'lakewave' { pos, count } is logged. sfx: for each open flower f in ctx.lotus.flowers (<= 6) triggerBell({ midi: pitchFor(f.note, 5), pos: f.bud, gain: 0.10, dur: 2.6, kind: 'glass', attack: 0.03, wet: 0.7, when: now + hypot(f.bud.x - head.x, f.bud.z - head.z) / 2.5, tag: 'wave' }) so the flowers sound in the order the wave reaches them, plus one pink-noise breath noiseBurst({ kind: 'pink', type: 'lowpass', freq: 600, q: 0.5, dur: 1.5, gain: 0.05, pos: head }) at the front's departure. ambience.js: S.offs.push(ctx.events.on('lakewave', () => startle(2, 4))) using the existing cricket hush. The existing aurora voice 3.2 s after the star lands just as the wave reaches the far cloud.
discoverability: Requires nothing beyond the taught lantern release; the star moment is already the experience's big payoff and this makes the whole lake acknowledge it. No hint text; if the player is looking at the sky they hear the flowers answer behind them and turn to see the wave finishing.
conflicts: Purely event-driven from 'lanternstar'; no hand state is read. Landed fireflies (LANDED/APPROACH/ESCORT/VISIT) are skipped by the pass, so a hand-full of fireflies keeps its steady glow and nothing about landing changes. Kuramoto is held for 6 s and then resumes; the clouds' long-period synchrony swells are unaffected afterwards. No pinch, no two-hand pose.
harnessStep: Restructure the existing fast-forward in the 'lantern-star' step: run clock.step = 0.1 frame by frame, polling events() each frame until 'lanternstar' appears (about frame 250), then set clock.step = 1/36 and sample 130 frames (3.6 s): record base = stats().fireflyMeanBright before the star (add `fireflyMeanBright: ctx.fireflies.meanBright`, a per-frame sum(bright)/N computed in the existing loop) and peak = max over the samples. Assert events().some(e => e.type === 'lakewave' && e.detail.count >= 100), peak > 2.5 * base (normally the mean sits ~0.1-0.2 because flashes are sparse; a third of a cloud flashing together lifts it well above that), and, since the lotus touch step runs later in the current order, either move the lotus step before the lantern step or assert on window.__nocturneCtx.lotus.flowers.some(f => f.waveAt > 0) only when any flower is open. Also check stats().drawCalls unchanged versus report.final baseline.
risks: Smallest feature; the risks are aesthetic. Overriding phase[] could produce a too-crisp 'blink' if the front is too fast: 2.5 m/s and the 0.15 s rise / 0.5 s decay give a ~1.5 m band, which reads as a ripple, but tune on device. At dt = 0.1 (harness fast-forward) the band is coarse, hence the switch back to 1/36 for the assertion. The wave overlaps the star's sparkle and the aurora voice; the 0.8 s delay and the bells' low gain (0.10) keep it under them, but the mix needs a listen. If Firefly escort is built, its spill-time sync kick and this wave's 6 s hold must not both run at once (hold wins).
angle: Ecology: the lake as one living system. Each feature is a loop between two of the things the player already loves (lotus, lanterns, fireflies), triggered only by interactions that already exist (setting a lantern down, releasing one, touching a bud, waiting for a star), so no new gesture is introduced and nothing can be confused with pinch-pull, the grab, the leave pose or firefly landing. All four add zero draw calls (new dynamic attributes on existing InstancedMesh/Points), allocate nothing per frame (typed arrays; Vector3.clone() only inside rare event emits, matching the existing lotus/lantern pattern), and are O(N) at most once per event. If more than one is built, coordinate the new firefly state numbers (ESCORT=4, VISIT=5, CARRY=6) and the shared `cause` key added to main.js summarize().

name: Koi under the surface
pitch: A small shoal of pale koi cruises beneath the water around you, gathering under the nearest floating lantern's light and drawing faint plankton trails as they pass. Rest a hand under the water and hold it still and one turns, glides over and noses your fingertip with a low soft note; sweep a hand fast through the water and they bolt, each dart writing a streak of plankton light across the surface.
gesture: APPROACH trigger (per hand, own timer stillWet[hi]): h.visible && h.submerged && h.still && !h.pinch.active && h.submergedDepth > 0.06; stillWet accrues while all hold, resets otherwise; at stillWet > 1.0 s recruit the nearest fish in state CRUISE with cooldown <= 0 within 2.5 m of h.tips[0] (index tip), then re-arm that hand's recruit timer 2.5 s (a second fish may follow). Target = h.tips[0] + (0, -0.03, 0), clamped to y <= level - 0.05. Approach speed 0.35 m/s easing to 0.10 m/s over the last 0.2 m, turn rate <= 2.5 rad/s, S-wobble 0.04 m. NIBBLE when nose within 0.04 m of the target and h.still: hold 1.5-3 s with a small wag, emit koinibble once, ctx.water.disturb(tip.x, tip.z, 0.04, 0.03) every 0.5 s while nibbling, energy += 0.03; then CRUISE with cooldown 8 s. Abort APPROACH (no dart) if h.still becomes false with h.palm.speed > 0.35, or the hand leaves the water. DART trigger: any h.visible && h.submerged && h.palm.speed > 0.7: every fish within 0.8 m of h.palm.position gets velocity 1.6 m/s along horizontal (fish - palm), state DART for 0.7 s (decay tau 0.6 s), cooldown 6 s; one koidart {pos: palm.clone(), hand, count} per hand per 0.5 s. Also lanternsplash within 1.2 m of a fish -> DART. Pinching hands (pinch.active) are ignored for APPROACH so pulling the world never summons a fish. Idle CRUISE: school centre orbits the head at 1.6 m (period 90 s), fish keep depth level-0.45..level-0.08 (ideal level-0.22), speed 0.15-0.35 m/s, separation 0.25 m (N<=7 so <=21 pairs), head-column avoidance radius 0.45; when no hand is submerged each fish drifts toward the nearest 'floating' lantern within 4 m and loiters 0.25 m under it. Every 0.4 s a cruising fish within 3 m of the head drops disturb(x, z, 0.06, 0.02) so the plankton carry it; a darting fish drops disturb(x, z, 0.05, 0.045) every 0.08 s while depth < 0.3 m (<= 3 queue entries per frame).
visual: One THREE.InstancedMesh 'koi' (N = 7, 5 when quality.tier === 'quest2'), renderOrder 1 (under the water, drawn before it like plankton so the surface tints it), opaque, depthWrite true, frustumCulled false. Geometry: LatheGeometry spindle profile (12 points x 10 segments) + a vertical tail-fin plane (2x3 segments) + two pectoral planes, merged with mergeGeometries, ~260 tris (7 instances ~1.8k tris). Instance attributes: aPhase, aWag (0..1, set from speed each frame), aLight (0..1 from nearest floating lantern: bright/(1+(d/0.5)^2)), aSeed (pattern choice), instanceMatrix from position/heading/pitch. Vertex shader (src/shaders/koi.js): body undulation x += sin(uTime*(6+10*aWag) + aPhase - v*4.0) * (0.006+0.02*aWag) * v*v with v = 0 nose..1 tail, tail plane gets an extra lag term; samples uSim = ctx.water.simTexture at fract(worldXZ/uTile) to pass sim.b*0.75+sim.a*1.3 as vGlow. Fragment: pattern from tex.noise sampled at uv*3+aSeed*7, thresholded into white / lantern-amber / near-black patches (three palettes by aSeed); white patches are 'moonlit' at 0.9 + vGlow*1.4 in planktonColor2 cyan so the fish reads through the 0.88-alpha water as a pale ghost lit by its own trail; moon Lambert (uMoonDir from scene 'moonLight') x0.35, aLight adds lantern amber to the upper body, depth darkening exp(-(level - y)*4), fogExp2 fade, then tonemapping/colorspace chunks. No mirror needed (under water). Draw calls +1. Per-frame CPU: typed arrays (pos, vel, heading, state, timer, cooldown), one Matrix4 compose per fish, zero allocations after init.
sound: Events: koinibble {pos: Vector3 clone of the fingertip, hand, index} and koidart {pos, hand, count} (append both to the eventLog list in main.js). sfx.js: koinibble -> playAt(S, 'plop_airy_1', pos, {gain 0.10, rate 0.7+0.1*rng, refDistance 0.8}) plus triggerBell({midi: pitchFor(S, floor(rng*3), 4), pos, gain 0.14, dur 2.0, kind 'ceramic', attack 0.03, tag 'koi'}) — a register below the lotus so fish sit under the flowers musically; notePlayed(S, midi) so the aurora may restate it. koidart -> noiseBurst(S, {pos, dur 0.18, gain 0.05 + 0.02*min(count,4), type 'lowpass', freq 900, sweepTo 350, q 0.7, kind 'pink'}) — a muffled underwater thump. ambience.js: koidart -> S.startle(2, 4) (a bolting fish hushes the crickets briefly, same language as the fast-hand startle). music.js: nothing. No new samples needed (plop_airy_1 is already in AUDIO_USED).
discoverability: The shoal is visible from the first minute as pale shapes and moving plankton smears under the near lanterns (they gather under lantern light, so anyone looking at a lantern sees them), and the existing water hint sends every hand into the lake anyway; the first still moment under water is answered within a few seconds. Hint entry (after the 'still' firefly hint in HINTS so the two stillness hints never overlap): { id: 'koi', text: 'rest a hand under the water and wait', after: 110, done: (ctx, s) => s.nibbled, ready: (ctx, s) => s.touchedWater } with s.nibbled set from koinibble.
conflicts: Both triggers require h.submerged, which fireflies (openStill needs !submerged) and the leave pose (neither hand submerged) already exclude, so a hand can never be summoning a fish and landing a firefly or leaving at once. Koi are not grabbables and the module ignores pinch.active hands for the approach, so a pinch-and-pull under water stays pure locomotion and a missed pinch still does nothing. The dart threshold (palm.speed > 0.7, submerged) is the same speed that already scatters fireflies above water and startles crickets under it, so fast-hands-scatter-life is one consistent rule rather than a new meaning. Fish avoid the head column and never surface, so they never enter the 13 cm grab radius of a lantern from above.
harnessStep: After 'calibrated' (rig y ~ -0.05, world level 0.95): setHand('right', [0.2, 0.72, -0.45], 0, { pitchDeg: -20 }) so all WATER_JOINTS sit ~25 cm under; frames(330) (9.2 s at 1/36: 1 s of stillWet + <= 2.5 m at 0.35 m/s). Assert step('koi-comes-to-still-hand', events().some(e => e.type === 'koinibble') && page.evaluate(() => window.__nocturneCtx.koi.nearestToHand) < 0.08, { koi: stats().koi, nibbles: stats().koiNibbles }). Then for i in 1..8: setHand('right', [0.2 - 0.5*i/8, 0.72, -0.45], 0, { pitchDeg: -20 }); frame() (0.5 m in 8 frames = 2.25 m/s); frames(4); assert step('koi-dart', events().some(e => e.type === 'koidart' && e.detail.count >= 1) && world().koi.some(k => k.state === 'dart')). main.js adds stats().koi = ctx.koi.count, stats().koiNibbles = ctx.koi.nibbles, and world().koi = list of {x, y, z, state}; ctx.koi = { count, nibbles, darts, nearestToHand, positions, states }.
risks: Visibility: everything under the surface reaches the eye at (1 - 0.88) of its tone-mapped colour plus the water's own colour, so a plain Lambert fish would vanish; the spec compensates with overbright white patches and the disturb-driven plankton trail, but the first build must be checked in a screenshot from the harness (koi.png) and W.alpha may need to drop to ~0.84 when a fish is within 2 m (a uniform, not a new pass). At grazing angles the water's Fresnel pushes alpha to 1 and distant fish disappear — acceptable (they are meant to be seen by looking down). Disturb budget: cruising + darting fish must stay under ~4 queued disturbances per frame so hand rings are never starved (hands fill slots first anyway). The approach path must respect the head column and pads so a fish never clips through a lotus pad from below (add pad avoidance radius 0.2 around ctx.lotus.pads within 1 m). Tuning of the 'ghost' look on Quest 2 (fewer fish, no anisotropy) is the main unknown.

name: Frogs on the lily pads
pitch: Three small frogs sit on the outermost lily pads of the nearest lotus clusters, croaking now and then and answering each lotus note with a low reply. Bring a slow hand near and one turns to watch you; touch its back and it leaps in an arc into the water with a plop and a ring, swims off as a streak of plankton light and climbs out onto another pad.
gesture: Per frog (state SIT): nearest visible hand h (h.visible) with horizontal distance d from h.palm.position to the frog. WATCH: d < 0.35 && h.palm.speed <= 0.55 -> the frog's yaw eases toward the hand (rate 3 rad/s), aAlert -> 1 (eyes brighten). STARTLE: d < 0.45 && h.palm.speed > 0.55 -> leap now (away from the hand). TOUCH: any h.tips[k] (k in 0..4) within 0.055 m of the frog body centre (pad point + (0, 0.02, 0)) -> leap. Leap: pick a target pad in the same cluster (ctx.lotus.pads with p.cluster === frog.cluster, not the current pad, farthest from the hand if startled, random otherwise; if the cluster has only one pad, land in open water 0.35 m away); ballistic arc with flight time 0.45-0.6 s (v0 solved from range and g = 9.81), body pitched along velocity; emit frogleap {pos: clone, hand, index, note} at takeoff (note = cluster % 6). Splashdown at y <= level: disturb(x, z, 0.10, 0.22), emit frogsplash {pos, index}, energy += 0.03; SWIM 0.06 m under the surface toward the target pad at 0.5 m/s (disturb(x, z, 0.06, 0.05) every 0.12 s); CLIMB 0.5 s from level-0.06 up to the pad (ease-out); SIT with touch cooldown 4 s. Croak schedule: every 9-20 s per frog while no visible hand is within 0.6 m (frogs go quiet when approached, like real ones), plus call-and-response: on lotusbloom the frog whose cluster === e.index croaks 0.6 s later with midi = pitchFor(note, 2); each croak drives aCroak (throat pulse 0.35 s) and emits frogcroak {pos, index, note}. Frogs read pad drift from ctx.lotus.pads[].x/z each frame (the frogs module registers after lotus in WORLD_MODULES).
visual: One THREE.InstancedMesh 'frogs' (3 instances), renderOrder 3 (above water), opaque, fog on. Geometry (~300 tris): a squashed body sphere (SphereGeometry 10x7 scaled 0.05 x 0.032 x 0.06), two eye spheres (r 0.011) tagged aPart=1, a throat sphere tagged aPart=2 that the vertex shader scales by 1 + 0.9*aCroak, instanceMatrix from pad point / yaw / leap pitch, instance attributes aCroak, aAlert, aLight (nearest floating lantern within 3 m: bright/(1+(d/0.6)^2)). Fragment (src/shaders/frogs.js): dark olive base (0x1c2e1a) with a moon rim (pow(1 - n.v, 3) * uMoonColor), a wet-sheen specular from uMoonDir, eyes (aPart==1) get an amber glint from aLight and brighten with aAlert (0.15 -> 0.6), fogExp2, tonemapping/colorspace chunks. While SWIM the frog is 6 cm under the surface at renderOrder 3, so the water's depth write hides it for free ('it dives and vanishes') and only its plankton wake shows; on CLIMB it re-emerges through the surface. Draw calls +1. No per-frame allocation: 3 state records with preallocated Vector3s, one Matrix4 compose per frog.
sound: Events: frogleap {pos, hand, index, note}, frogsplash {pos, index}, frogcroak {pos, index, note} (append to the eventLog list). sfx.js: frogcroak -> new helper croak(S, {pos, midi, dur 0.3}): sawtooth oscillator at mtof(midi) (midi 38-45, D2..A2) -> lowpass 700 Hz Q 2 -> gate gain driven by a 24-32 Hz square LFO (0.5 + 0.5*lfo, the rattle) -> envelope (attack 0.03, hold, release 0.12) -> api.spatial({pos, refDistance 0.8, out: world}), gain 0.08, nodes disconnected onended; the response croak after lotusbloom uses the lotus note two octaves down so the frog 'answers' in key. frogleap -> noiseBurst(S, {pos, dur 0.04, gain 0.05, type 'highpass', freq 2500, q 0.7}) (the pad flexes). frogsplash -> playAt(S, 'plop_airy_1', pos, {gain 0.35, rate 0.9+0.2*rng, refDistance 1.2}) + disturb already rings the water. ambience.js: frogsplash -> S.startle(3, 5). music.js: nothing. No new samples (plop_airy_1 already decoded; croaks are synthesized like the crickets).
discoverability: The croaks are spatial and come from the near cluster 0.65 m front-left from the first minute, the eyes carry an amber glint from the nearest lantern, and the head-turn when a slow hand approaches makes the frog announce itself; the existing lotus hint already sends fingertips into the cluster. Hint entry: { id: 'frog', text: 'something small is watching from the lily pads', after: 130, done: (ctx, s) => s.frogLeapt, ready: (ctx, s) => s.bloomed && nearestLotus(ctx) < REACH + 0.15 } with s.frogLeapt set from frogleap.
conflicts: Frogs are touch-only (fingertip within 5.5 cm) and are never grabbables, so a pinch near a frog is a pinchmiss and then locomotion exactly as the sanctioned rule requires; no pinch semantics are added. The startle at palm.speed > 0.55 is the same fast-hand-scatters-life rule as fireflies (0.7) and koi. A still open hand near a frog does nothing to it (it only watches), so firefly landing on that same hand is unaffected. Frogs sit on the pad farthest from the cluster centre (>= 0.2 m from the bud), so a fingertip touching the bud (0.08 m radius) cannot also be within 0.055 m of the frog; if a large hand does both, the outcome is a bloom plus a leap, both harmless. The leave pose is two palms together above open water, never near pads.
harnessStep: After the 'lotus-bloomed' step: const F = (await world()).frogs[0] (cluster 0, within reach; world() adds frogs: [{x, y, z, state, cluster}]). setHand('right', [F.x, F.y + 0.28, F.z + 0.15], 0, { pitchDeg: 0 }) (wrist 15 cm behind, fingers along -Z put the index tip over the frog); frames(10); then for i in 1..30: setHand('right', [F.x, F.y + 0.28 - 0.26*i/30, F.z + 0.15], 0, { pitchDeg: 0 }); frame() (0.31 m/s, below the 0.55 startle speed so only the touch can fire). Assert step('frog-leaps-when-touched', events().some(e => e.type === 'frogleap' && e.detail.index === 0) && ['leap','swim','climb'].includes(world().frogs[0].state)). frames(80); assert step('frog-splash-and-return', events().some(e => e.type === 'frogsplash') && ['swim','climb','sit'].includes(world().frogs[0].state), { frogs: stats().frogs }). A separate check that the lotusbloom earlier produced a frogcroak with index 0 within 1 s: events().some(e => e.type === 'frogcroak' && e.detail.index === 0).
risks: Placement depends on ctx.lotus.pads geometry: with 3-5 pads per cluster the farthest pad from the centre is 0.25-0.4 m out, but the harness must confirm the frog is never inside the bud's 8 cm touch radius. The leap must not land on the flower itself (exclude pads within 0.2 m of the bud as targets). Under-surface hiding relies on the water's depthWrite true and renderOrder 2 staying as they are (documented in water.js). The croak synth needs care to stay 'frog' and not 'buzzer' (short, low, rattly, 0.08 gain, spatial) and must go quiet when a hand is near or it will feel like a toy. Frogs on far clusters (1.4-3.8 m) only become reachable after wading, which is fine but means two of three are scenery until then.

name: Moon jelly for the calm
pitch: When you stay completely still — head and hands — a moon jellyfish that has been drifting out in the dark rises slowly to hover just under the surface in front of you, its bell glowing softly through the water while long tentacles trail beneath. Touch its bell and a ring of light runs down it with a low bowl tone; cup a still palm beneath it under the water and it settles into your hand and breathes there.
gesture: INVITE: ctx.calm > 0.6 sustained for 3 s (own timer; calm already means head < 0.08 m/s, both hands stillDisp <= 0.05, no pull) while state IDLE and cooldown <= 0 -> state RISE: target = head + cameraForwardHorizontal*0.55 with apex at level - 0.08; drift speed 0.3 m/s with pulses, arrives in <= 9 s from <= 2.8 m; emit jellyrise {pos} on arrival -> HOVER. HOVER holds while ctx.calm > 0.3 || any hand is h.still; STARTLE if a visible hand with h.palm.speed > 0.7 comes within 0.6 m of the apex: 3 fast pulses, sink to level - 0.5 and glide away (SINK -> IDLE, cooldown 40 s). TOUCH (RISE or HOVER): any h.visible hand's h.tips[k] within 0.06 m of the apex, or h.submerged && h.palm.position within 0.08 m of the apex, with >= 0.6 s since the last touch -> emit jellytouch {pos: apex clone, hand, index: touchCount}: uRing runs apex->rim over 0.8 s, glow x2.2 decaying over 3 s, one strong pulse with a 0.12 m/s kick away from the hand, ctx.water.disturb(x, z, 0.16, 0.10), energy += 0.05; touches step through ctx.music.currentChord.midi (chord tones) so a run of touches arpeggiates the chord; after 5 touches within 20 s a long glow then SINK (cooldown 60 s). REST (HOVER only): a hand with h.visible && h.submerged && h.still && !h.pinch.active && h.palm.normal.y > 0.5 (palm up) whose palm.position is within 0.15 m below the apex for 1.0 s -> the apex follows h.palm.position + h.palm.normal*0.06 with lag (tau 0.6 s), glow breathes (period 3.2 s), emit jellyrest {hand} once, ctx.jelly.restingHand = h; leaves (SINK, cooldown 30 s) when h.palm.speed > 0.35, the hand leaves the water, or after 12 s. IDLE: a slow circuit around the player at 1.5-2.8 m, apex depth level - 0.35, pulse every 2.4 s giving a 0.05 m/s kick along heading, drag 0.8/s, never within 0.9 m unless invited. While the apex is < 0.12 m under the surface, disturb(x, z, 0.16, 0.02) every 0.3 s so the surface bioluminescence marks it from above.
visual: Two draw calls. (1) Bell: one Mesh, SphereGeometry(1, 24, 12, 0, 2PI, 0, PI/2) hemisphere scaled 0.18 x 0.12 x 0.18, ShaderMaterial (src/shaders/jelly.js) transparent, AdditiveBlending, depthWrite false, side DoubleSide, renderOrder 1 (under the water, before it). Vertex: contraction p.xz *= 1 - 0.12*uPulse*(1 - p.y), p.y += 0.04*uPulse (uPulse = smooth envelope from the CPU pulse phase), rim flutter 0.01*sin(uTime*2 + atan(p.z,p.x)*8). Fragment: fresnel rim pow(1 - |n.v|, 2.5)*0.6 in mix(planktonColor2 0x9fffe0, 0xdfe8ff), four horseshoe gonads as a procedural ring pattern in uv (0.25 intensity, the moon-jelly hallmark), uRing = a bright band at |ringT - height| < 0.08 travelling apex->rim after a touch, uGlow multiplies everything, depth darkening exp(-(level - y)*3), tonemapping/colorspace chunks. (2) Tentacles + oral arms: one THREE.Points of 24 x 14 = 336 points with attributes aTent (angle index) and aT (0..1 along the tentacle), renderOrder 1, additive; the vertex shader builds each point from uCentre + rim point at radius 0.17 rotated by aTent, y -= aT*0.45, xz += 0.03*sin(uTime*1.3 + aTent*7 + aT*5)*aT and a velocity lag -uVel*aT*0.6 (uVel from the CPU), size 0.012*uPixelScale/depth, brightness uGlow*(1 - aT*0.6)*0.5, sprite tex.glowSoft. No CPU tentacle sim, no allocation. On Quest 2 tentacle count 16 x 12.
sound: Events: jellyrise {pos}, jellytouch {pos, hand, index}, jellyrest {hand} (append to the eventLog list). sfx.js: jellyrise -> noiseBurst(S, {pos, dur 1.2, gain 0.04, type 'lowpass', freq 300, sweepTo 180, q 0.6, kind 'pink', refDistance 1.0}) — a breath from below. jellytouch -> midi = chord tone chordMidi[index % chordMidi.length] placed in register 4 (ctx.music.currentChord.midi, else pitchFor(S, index, 4)); layer = pickTuned(S, BOWLS, midi, 7) -> playAt(S, layer.name, pos, {gain 0.22, rate: layer.rate, refDistance 1.5, out: chimes}); plus triggerBell({midi: midi - 12, pos, gain 0.12, dur 3.5, index 0, attack 0.05, tag 'jelly'}) (a pure sine sub under the bowl); notePlayed(S, midi). music.js: jellyrest -> requestSwell('pad_bioluminescence', 0.3). ambience.js: nothing (the jelly is the calm reward; the existing calm drone already fades in alongside it). No new samples.
discoverability: The jelly is visible from the start as a faint glowing dome drifting 2-3 m out, and the calm drone plus plankton breathing already reward stillness, so the first quiet minute brings it in unannounced; its surface bioluminescence marks it as it approaches. Hint entry: { id: 'jelly', text: 'be still and something will rise', after: 160, done: (ctx, s) => s.jellyRose, ready: (ctx, s) => s.touchedWater && ctx.calm < 0.2 } with s.jellyRose set from jellyrise; the hint never shows while the player is already calm, so it never nags someone doing the right thing.
conflicts: The invitation is ctx.calm (whole-body stillness, an existing reward channel), not a hand gesture, so nothing the hands do is reinterpreted. Touch is fingertip proximity to a non-grabbable, so a pinch near the bell is a pinchmiss and then locomotion, per the rule; no new meaning for pinch-and-move. REST requires h.submerged and palm-up, which fireflies (openStill needs !submerged) and the leave pose (neither hand submerged, palms facing each other) already exclude. STARTLE at palm.speed > 0.7 is the shared fast-hand rule. If the koi proposal also ships, koi skip a hand for which ctx.jelly.restingHand === h, so the two stillness rewards never fight over one hand; the koi answer a single still hand, the jelly answers a still body.
harnessStep: Right after 'calibrated' with both hands parked at [+-0.25, 1.25, -0.4] (fake head is static, so ctx.calm rises 0.25/s): frames(110) then assert page.evaluate(() => window.__nocturneCtx.calm) > 0.6; frames(330) (9.2 s, enough for <= 2.8 m at 0.3 m/s); const J = (await world()).jelly (world() adds jelly: {x, y, z, state, glow}); assert step('jelly-rises-for-calm', events().some(e => e.type === 'jellyrise') && J.state === 'hover' && Math.hypot(J.x - head[0], J.z - head[2]) < 0.8 && (0.95 - J.y) < 0.15). name: Moths around the lanterns
pitch: Pale moths spiral around the nearest lanterns, flashing white as they cross the flame, and they follow a lantern you lift, tightening into a cloud and settling on the paper when you hold it still. Move it quickly and they burst away with a soft flutter, and when you release a lantern to rise they chase it a few metres into the sky before spiralling back to the next light.
gesture: No new hand gesture: moths respond to lantern state and the existing fast-hand rule. Assignment (every 0.5 s, like the crackle slots): the 3 nearest lanterns from ctx.lanterns.list with state 'floating' or 'held', or 'rising' with position.y - level < 2.5, within 6 m of the head; moths (N = 40, 28 on quest2) split evenly, others idle at their last lantern's position dimmed. ORBIT: each moth circles L.top with radius r = 0.12 + 0.18*seed oscillating +-0.08 (spiral), angular speed 2-4 rad/s, vertical bob 0.08 m, plus sum-of-sines jitter (<= 0.5 m/s). SETTLE: when L.state === 'held' && L.held.still (the holding hand's still flag) for 1.5 s, orbit radius scales x0.6 and up to 3 moths per lantern enter SETTLED: stuck to the paper at (yaw theta, height h) => L.position + rotate(theta)*RADIUS*1.02 + up*h, moving with the lantern, for 2-6 s; emit mothsettle {pos: L.position clone, count} once per settle wave; floating lanterns also get settles at a slower rate (every 6-12 s). SCATTER: L.state === 'held' && L.held.palm.speed > 0.6, or any h.visible hand with h.palm.speed > 0.7 within 0.4 m of a moth -> burst outward at 0.8 m/s, SCATTER 1 s, then re-orbit; emit mothflutter {pos, count} rate-limited to one per 0.5 s. FOLLOW UP: a 'rising' lantern keeps its moths (they orbit L.top as it climbs) until position.y - level > 2.5, then each peels off (SCATTER with a downward bias) and is reassigned. Flame cross: whenever a moth's horizontal distance to the lantern axis < 0.05 m its brightness spikes to 1 for 0.1 s (backlit wings) — computed in the vertex shader from uLantern positions, no CPU work.
visual: One THREE.Points 'moths', renderOrder 4, N = 40 (28 on quest2), attributes position (dynamic), aBright, aSeed, aLantern (index 0..2 of its lantern or -1). ShaderMaterial (src/shaders/moths.js) with uniforms uLantern[3] (vec4: xyz of L.top, w = bright), uPixelScale, uMaxPx 40, uTime, uFogDensity, sprite tex.glowSoft; NormalBlending with premultiplied pale grey-cream colour (0xd8d2c0) so they read as bodies, not lights: brightness = uLantern[i].w / (1 + (d/0.35)^2) * aBright, flame-cross spike when d_axis < 0.05, size 0.02 m world (wing flicker: size *= 0.7 + 0.3*sin(uTime*40 + aSeed*50)), fogExp2 fade, tonemapping/colorspace chunks. No mirror. Draw calls +1. CPU: typed arrays (pos, vel, state, lantern, angle, timer), O(N) per frame plus the 0.5 s assignment over <= 24 lanterns, zero allocation.
sound: Events: mothsettle {pos, count}, mothflutter {pos, count} (append to the eventLog list). sfx.js: mothflutter -> new helper flutter(S, {pos, dur 0.25, count}): pink noise -> bandpass 1800 Hz Q 2 -> gate gain driven by a 28 Hz square LFO (0.5 + 0.5*lfo) -> envelope (attack 0.01, release 0.08) -> api.spatial({pos, refDistance 0.7}), gain 0.04 + 0.01*min(count, 4) (the same LFO-gate helper the frog croak uses, different source and band). mothsettle -> two noiseBurst ticks 40 ms apart (dur 0.012, gain 0.03, highpass 3500, q 0.7) at the lantern — paper. ambience.js and music.js: nothing; the existing lantern crackle already sits under the cloud.

No hint entry: this is ambient discovery, and a hint would spend the one-hint-at-a-time budget on something the eye already finds.
conflicts: Moths never land on hands, so firefly landing keeps sole ownership of the open-still-hand reward; the settle uses the holding hand's still flag only while a lantern is already grabbed, which is a state locomotion can never be in (pulling requires !grabbed). No grabbable is added and pinch is never read, so pinch-and-pull and missed pinches are untouched. The scatter threshold (palm.speed > 0.7) is the existing fast-hand rule. The leave pose involves no lantern and both hands still, so the only effect is moths continuing to orbit floating lanterns.
harnessStep: Inside the existing lantern step, after 'lantern-grabbed' and before the lift: hold the pinch still with setHand('right', [L.x, L.y + 0.12, L.z], 1) and frames(80) (2.2 s > the 1.5 s settle hold); assert step('moths-settle-on-still-lantern', events().some(e => e.type === 'mothsettle') && page.evaluate(() => window.__nocturneCtx.moths.settled) >= 1, { orbiting: stats().mothsOrbiting }). Then for i in 1..6: setHand('right', [L.x + 0.5*i/6, L.y + 0.12, L.z], 1); frame() (0.5 m in 6 frames = 3 m/s); frames(4); assert step('moths-scatter-from-fast-lantern', events().some(e => e.type === 'mothflutter') && page.evaluate(() => window.__nocturneCtx.moths.settled) === 0 && page.evaluate(() => window.__nocturneCtx.moths.scattered) > 0). Then return the hand to [L.x, L.y + 0.12, L.z] and continue the existing lift/release; after 'lantern-released' and 40 frames assert page.evaluate(() => window.__nocturneCtx.moths.following) >= 1 (moths still bound to the rising lantern below 2.5 m). main.js adds stats().moths = ctx.moths.count, stats().mothsOrbiting, and ctx.moths = { count, settled, scattered, following, positions, states }.

Payoff is ambient rather than a new thing to do with the hands, which is why it scores lowest; it is the cheapest of the four and pairs best with the koi (fish under the light, moths above it) if only two are built.

name: Water writing
pitch: Skim one fingertip slowly along the surface and it leaves a thread of plankton light that lingers for ten seconds, each stretch of the line ringing a soft pentatonic note (left of you is low, right is high). Lift the finger and a pulse runs back along the line singing it again; close the line into a loop around a lotus cluster and every bud inside opens in turn.
gesture: Per hand h, every frame: h.visible && h.active && !h.pinch.active && !h.grabbed; lowest valid tip k* = argmin y over h.tips[k] with h.joints[TIP_NAMES[k]].valid; tip depth (ctx.water.level - tip.y) in [-0.005, 0.06]; palm hovering: h.palm.position.y - level >= 0.05; world horizontal speed hypot(h.palm.velocity.x, h.palm.velocity.z) in [0.04, 0.6] m/s. Conditions true 3 consecutive frames -> trace starts (traceId++). While drawing: emit a point when the tip has moved >= 0.015 m from the last point (world xz, y = level + 0.015). Note rule: degree = clamp(floor((az + 60deg) / 15deg), 0, 7) where az = signed angle between the camera's horizontal forward (camera.getWorldDirection into a preallocated Vector3) and (point - headWorld).xz; a note fires when degree changes or 0.2 m of arc has passed since the last note, min interval 0.1 s -> 'watertrace' { hand, pos: new Vector3, note: degree, index: traceId }. End: conditions fail 4 consecutive frames, tip depth > 0.08 (plunged) or speed > 0.6 (a splash) -> 'watertraceend' { hand, count: notes, index }; if notes >= 2 an echo is scheduled at t + 0.8 s: a cursor walks the trace's arc at 0.35 m/s and re-fires each stored note as 'waterecho' { pos, note, index }. Loop close: arc >= 0.45 m and dist(tip.xz, first point.xz) < 0.10 -> 'watercircle' { pos: centroid (new Vector3), count: buds inside, index }: point-in-polygon over this trace's points for each closed lotus bud (ctx.lotus.flowers[i].open false), ctx.lotus.open(i) staggered 0.18 s apart from a preallocated 6-slot queue, 5 disturbs (centroid + 4 at half the loop radius, radius 0.3, strength 0.06) for a flash of plankton inside the loop, ctx.energy += 0.05, then the trace ends and echoes as usual.
visual: One THREE.Points over a pool of 2 x 384 slots (ring buffer per hand, oldest overwritten; at 0.6 m/s and 0.015 m spacing that is 40 pts/s, so a 10 s life never wraps). Attributes: position (3), aBorn, aArc, aHand, aTrace (all Float32, DynamicDrawUsage, needsUpdate only on frames that add points). Age and brightness are computed in the vertex shader from uTime - aBorn (rise 0.15 s, hold 4 s, fade to 11 s, a slow shimmer 0.75 + 0.25 sin(uTime*3 + aArc*20)); dead slots (aBorn = -1e9) collapse out of clip like drips. Echo pulse: uniform uEcho[2] = vec4(traceId, arc, gain, 0); a point with abs(aTrace - uEcho[h].x) < 0.5 adds gain * exp(-((aArc - arc)/0.08)^2) * 1.5. Sprite: glowFirefly map, world size 0.03 m, perspective px = size * uPixelScale / depth, min 2 px, max 40 px, plankton colours mixed by hash(aArc), additive, depthWrite false, depthTest true, renderOrder 3 at level + 0.015 (above the sim's max 2.1 cm crests), fog as brightness attenuation like fireflies. points.visible only while the newest point is younger than 11 s, so 0 draw calls at rest, +1 while a line lives. CPU per frame: O(1) per hand plus the echo cursor's O(points passed). No allocation except the per-note event Vector3 (the lotus/lantern pattern).
sound: sfx.js: 'watertrace' -> triggerBell({ midi: pitchFor(S, note, 5), pos, gain 0.14, dur 1.8, kind 'glass', wet 0.3, tag 'trace' }) and notePlayed(midi) so the aurora voice can restate a drawn phrase; 'waterecho' -> triggerBell({ same midi, pos, gain 0.08, dur 2.4, kind 'ceramic', wet 0.6, refDistance 1.2 }) — softer and wetter, the water answering from further away; 'watercircle' -> three ascending glass bells pitchFor(d0+i, 6) 0.11 s apart, gain 0.1, wet 0.6, plus noiseBurst({ pos, dur 0.25, gain 0.08, bandpass 500 -> 1400 Hz, q 2, kind 'pink' }) as the loop fills with light; the staggered lotusbloom bells that follow form the chord on their own. The existing per-hand swish plays quietly under the skimming fingertip (it is submerged at 0.3 m/s) and the drips module bursts when the finger lifts. music.js / ambience.js: no change.
discoverability: Anyone who dabbles a fingertip finds it within a second (the first note rings immediately); the ripple glow the sim already draws under the finger leads straight into the line. Hint (hints.js HINTS): { id: 'trace', text: 'draw on the water with one finger', after: 110, ready: s.touchedWater, done: s.traced } where s.traced is set by a 'watertraceend' with count >= 3. The loop bloom is a secret for players who circle the flowers; the echo teaches itself.
conflicts: No pinch is involved and a pinch (h.pinch.active) or a held object aborts the trace, so pinch-and-pull and the grab keep their exact meaning; the missed-pinch spark/tick is untouched. The palm must hover >= 5 cm above the water with only fingertips in it, which a plunged, stroking or paddling hand never satisfies (its palm is at or below the surface) and which is disjoint from Hush (palm within 2.5 cm of the surface) and Stir (palm below level + 0.02). The tracing hand is submerged (tip > 1 cm) so fireflies never try to land on it and the leave gesture (both hands not submerged, palms facing) cannot be matched. The lotus touch still works as before (fingertip near a bud opens it); loop-bloom only adds a second way to open buds.
harnessStep: Add 'watertrace', 'watertraceend', 'waterecho', 'watercircle' to the eventLog list and expose ctx.trace = { live, traces, notes, circles, active: [bool,bool] } via stats().trace. Step 'water-writing-sings': const L = s.water (0.95); setHand('right', [0.15, L + 0.09, -0.45], 0, { pitchDeg: -25, rollDeg: 0, curl: 0.15 }); frames(8); then for i = 1..60: setHand('right', [0.15 - 0.5*i/60, L + 0.09, -0.45], 0, same extra); frame() — with pitch -25 the fake tips sit at L - 0.017 (in the band) and the palm at L + 0.079, and 0.5 m over 60 frames at 1/36 s is 0.30 m/s; the sweep spans ~44 deg of azimuth = 3 note degrees. Assert events().filter(type === 'watertrace').length >= 3, distinct detail.note values >= 2, stats().trace.live >= 20, and world().rig unchanged (no locomotion). Step 'water-writing-echo': setHand('right', [-0.35, L + 0.35, -0.45], 0); frames(90); assert a 'watertraceend' with detail.count >= 3 and >= 2 'waterecho' events. Step 'water-circle-opens-buds': take the nearest closed bud B from world().lotus; for i = 0..105: a = 2*PI*i/100; setHand('right', [B.x + 0.22*cos(a), L + 0.09, B.z + 0.154 + 0.22*sin(a)], 0, { pitchDeg: -25, curl: 0.15 }); frame() (the fingertip is 0.154 m ahead of the wrist, so the tip circles B at 0.22 m at 0.5 m/s, never within the 0.08 m touch radius); frames(40); assert a 'watercircle' event with detail.count >= 1 followed by a 'lotusbloom' with detail.index === B.index.
risks: Real fingers dip deeper than the tidy fake one, so the depth band is generous (6 cm) and a 4-frame grace bridges tracking jitter; a thread drawn through a lantern's body shows through nothing because the trace is depth-tested. Bell density is bounded (<= ~6 notes/s plus the echo) inside the 8-voice pool. Points at 0.03 m are small on Quest 2; the min-2-px hold-up used by drips keeps them visible. The loop test relies on the trace ending within 0.10 m of its start; a sloppy loop simply echoes without blooming.
angle: gesture — the hands as instruments on the water: a finger that writes light and is sung back, a palm that carries a pool of it, a palm that stills the lake into a mirror, a hand that stirs the lights into a whirl

name: Cupped light
pitch: Cup a hand under the surface, palm up, and lift it slowly: a pool of plankton light comes up with it and sits glowing in your palm. Tilt the hand and it pours out as bright drops that ring the water; hold it level and still and fireflies come down to drink from it.
gesture: Per hand: charge accumulates while h.submerged && h.palm.normal.y > 0.3 (cap 0.7 s), clears 0.3 s after leaving the water. Form: the palm crosses the surface upward (prev h.palm.position.y <= level && now > level) with h.palm.normal.y > 0.6, h.meanCurl in [0.30, 0.72] (cupped: not open, below graspOn 0.75), !h.pinch.active, !h.grabbed, h.palm.velocityLocal.y in (0.03, 0.6) m/s (a slow lift; a fast one throws the water off), charge >= 0.15 -> fill = clamp(charge/0.5, 0.35, 1), 'cupfill' { hand, pos: palm.clone(), fill }, ctx.energy += 0.03. Holding: tilt = clamp((0.92 - h.palm.normal.y) / 0.5, 0, 1); pour = fill * tilt * 2.5 per second (a 40 deg tilt drains in ~1.3 s); a level palm only leaks 1/25 per second. Spill (dump at 6/s): h.meanCurl < 0.22 or > 0.80 held 0.15 s (fingers opened or a fist), h.pinch.active, h.palm.speed > 1.0, !h.visible; dipping back under (h.submerged) empties it silently and recharges. Drops: acc += pour * 14 * dt; each whole drop calls ctx.drips.spawnAt(x, y, z, vx, vy, vz, bright, handIndex) — a new 12-line public entry in drips.js that takes a free pool slot exactly like its internal spawn — at rim = palm.position + n*0.012 + d*0.045 with d = normalize(g - (g.n) n), g = (0,-1,0) (downhill on the palm plane; random horizontal if n.y > 0.995), velocity d*0.12 + (0,-0.05,0), bright = 0.2 + 0.8*fill. 'cuppour' { hand, pos } once per pour episode (re-armed after pour < 0.02 for 0.5 s). Fireflies: in fireflies.js hf.attract[hi] = ok && (hs.openStill || (ctx.cup.fill[hi] > 0.5 && hs.stillFor > 1.0)); hf.approach[hi] = ok && (hs.open || ctx.cup.fill[hi] > 0.3) && hs.speed <= 0.35 (3 lines; stillFor already counts still-and-not-submerged).
visual: One draw call: a 2-instance InstancedBufferGeometry of a CircleGeometry(1, 24) with per-instance aCenter (palm + normal*0.008), aNormal, aFill, aTilt, aDown (the downhill direction) and aSeed; the vertex shader builds a tangent basis from aNormal (t1 = normalize(cross(n, |n.y| < 0.9 ? up : x)), t2 = cross(n, t1)) and places the disc in the palm plane at radius 0.045 * (0.45 + 0.55*fill) with a 4 mm slosh (sin(uTime*3 + aSeed) * fill) and a cheap wobble of the rim; fragment: brightness fill * (0.8 + 0.2 sin(uTime*2.7 + seed)) * (1 - r^2)^1.5 in plankton colours (glowSoft map for the core), plus a bright crescent on the downhill side (max(dot(uv, aDown), 0) * tilt * 0.6) so the pouring edge lights up; additive, depthWrite false, depthTest true, renderOrder 4. mesh.visible only while max fill > 0.01 (0 draw calls at rest). The poured water itself is the existing drips Points (already budgeted, only visible while drops fall), so the pour rings the sim and plips through the existing landing path. The hand's glass shader is untouched.
sound: sfx.js: 'cupfill' -> noiseBurst({ pos, dur 0.14, gain 0.10, bandpass 500 -> 1100 Hz, q 2, kind 'pink' }) (a soft wet scoop) + triggerBell({ midi: pitchFor(S, 2, 5), pos, gain 0.08, dur 1.2, kind 'glass', wet 0.3 }) as the light settles; 'cuppour' -> noiseBurst({ pos, dur 0.35, gain 0.07, bandpass 2400 -> 1600 Hz, q 2.5 }); continuous trickle: in the 30 Hz swish control loop, const pour = ctx.cup?.pour?.[i] || 0; if (pour > 0.02) { g = max(g, smoothstep(0.02, 0.6, pour) * 0.16 * nearAtten(palm, head)); bp.frequency -> 2200 Hz } (the per-hand HRTF swish node doubles as the trickle, 4 lines). Every drop that lands emits the existing rate-limited 'drip' plip. Fireflies landing on the cup ring their usual bells. music.js / ambience.js: no change.
discoverability: Hands come up palm-up out of the water all the time and the existing drips burst already suggests water in the hand; the first slow palm-up lift with slightly curled fingers fills the cup. Hint: { id: 'cup', text: 'cup some water and lift it out', after: 120, ready: s.touchedWater, done: s.cupped } with s.cupped set by a 'cupfill' whose fill >= 0.6. Fireflies drinking is discovered by anyone who admires the pool for a few seconds (stillFor > 1 s).
conflicts: Pinch-and-pull: a pinch spills the cup and the cup needs a curl band that keeps the thumb and index ~7 cm apart; pinching while carrying water just spills it and then pulls as usual. Leave: needs both palms facing each other and within 9 cm; a palm-up cupped hand cannot satisfy fa/fb. Fireflies: the cupped hand is deliberately not 'open', so nothing changes for open hands; the added attract condition only fires with fill > 0.5, and the existing repel/leave-on-motion rules still apply. Lanterns: attraction requires h.open, so a cup does not tug lanterns. angle: gesture — the hands as instruments on the water: a finger that writes light and is sung back, a palm that carries a pool of it, a palm that stills the lake into a mirror, a hand that stirs the lights into a whirl

name: Hush
pitch: Rest an open palm flat on the water and keep it there: after a moment a circle of perfect stillness spreads out from under your hand, ripples die at its edge and the stars come up through the glass-still disc. The plankton go quiet, a low bowl note holds, raindrop notes begin to fall, and lifting the hand lets the lake breathe again.
gesture: Per hand: pose = h.visible && h.active && h.open && h.palm.normal.y < -0.8 && h.palm.position.y in [level - 0.05, level + 0.03] && h.still && !h.pinch.active && !h.grabbed (h.still is computed every frame from the filtered palm ring regardless of submersion; submersion itself is not required, the palm pads normally dip). hold += dt while pose, else hold = max(0, hold - 3*dt). At hold >= 0.6 the circle activates: centre locked to the palm xz (then lerped toward the palm at 1/s so drift does not drag it), strength s -> 1 with tau 0.8 s while the pose holds, radius r eased 0.25 -> 1.2 m over 3 s (easeOutCubic). When the pose breaks s decays with tau 1.2 s and r shrinks with s; 'hush' { hand, pos: palm.clone() } when s crosses 0.05 upward, 'hushend' { hand } when it falls below 0.02 after being active. Two circles (one per hand). Each frame the module also raises ctx.water.calm = max(ctx.water.calm, 0.6 * s) after player.js has set it (modules run after playerCtl.update), which feeds the existing calm rewards (plankton breathing, stronger global damping, calm drone). ctx.hush = { strength: max over hands, circles: [{ x, z, r, s, active }, ...], count }.

name: Stir
pitch: Circle a submerged hand slowly and the lake begins to turn with it: a whirl of plankton motes spirals around the centre, the glow in the water rotates, and any lantern floating nearby is carried gently around the eddy. Stop and the whirl unwinds over a few seconds.
gesture: Per hand: h.visible && h.active && h.submerged && h.palm.position.y < level + 0.02 && !h.pinch.active && !h.grabbed && h.palm.speedH >= 0.15 m/s. Heading theta = atan2(h.palm.velocityLocal.z, h.palm.velocityLocal.x); delta = wrapPi(theta - thetaPrev); if |delta| < 1.2 rad (no reversal) turn += delta, with turn *= exp(-dt/3) every frame (a 3 s leaky integrator). Stirring starts when |turn| >= 1.5*PI (a 0.5 rev/s circle gets there in 1.5 s, radius 5–25 cm) -> 'stir' { hand, pos: centre.clone(), speed: revs/s }; sign = sign(turn). Centre = mean of the last 24 palm samples taken 0.1 s apart (preallocated Float32Array ring; the mean of positions around a circle is its centre), omega = smoothed delta/dt (rad/s, signed), strength s -> min(1, |turn| / (2*PI)) with tau 0.5 s. Stops when speedH < 0.1 for 0.5 s, the hand leaves the water, or a pinch starts -> stirring false, s and omega decay with tau 3 s, 'stirend' { hand } when s < 0.02. Sim: every 0.08 s while s > 0.05, psi += omega*dt and two disturbs at centre + (cos psi, sin psi) * 0.22 and its opposite (radius 0.08, strength 0.05*s) so the plankton glow visibly rotates. ctx.stir = { vortices: [{ x, z, omega, s, active }, ...], strength, count }.
visual: One THREE.Points of 2 x 96 motes (192 points; positions, aBright, aSeed typed arrays; the fireflies pattern). Per mote a polar state (phi, r in [0.06, 0.40]); per frame while a vortex has s > 0.01: phi += omega * pow(0.3 / max(r, 0.15), 0.7) * dt (differential rotation, faster near the centre), r -= 0.03 * s * dt wrapping back to 0.40 below 0.05 (a slow inward spiral), position = centre + (cos phi, sin phi) * r at y = level + 0.01, brightness = s * (0.5 + 0.5 sin(uTime*4 + seed*30)) * (1 - r/0.45). Sprite: glowFirefly map, 0.025 m world size, perspective sizing with the shared min-px hold-up, plankton colours, additive, depthWrite false, depthTest true, renderOrder 3. points.visible only while max s > 0.01 (0 draw calls at rest, +1 while stirring). Lanterns: in the floating branch of lanterns.js, for each vortex with s > 0.05 and d = dist(P, centre) < 1.2: tangent = (-dz, dx)/d * sign(omega); vt = min(0.15, |omega| * 0.3 * s * clamp(0.35/d, 0, 1)); vx += tangent.x*vt - dx/d*0.02*s; vz += tangent.y*vt - dz/d*0.02*s (~8 lines; capped so a lantern never races).
sound: sfx.js: 'stir' -> playAt(S, 'whoosh_twirl_1', pos, { gain 0.16, rate 0.85, refDistance 1.2 }) (add 'whoosh_twirl_1' to AUDIO_USED in src/audio/index.js; the file is already on disk) ; continuous: in the 30 Hz per-hand swish block, const sv = ctx.stir?.vortices?.[i]?.s || 0; the band-pass centre gets + 500 * sv Hz and the gain floor max(g, 0.12 * sv * nearAtten) so the swish keeps spinning, brighter, for the few seconds the eddy unwinds after the hand pauses (3 lines). The existing swish already follows the circling hand and the lantern hull ripples plip as they are carried. music.js / ambience.js: no change (a fast stroke > 1.0 m/s already startles the crickets by the existing rule).
discoverability: Circling a hand in glowing water is one of the first things people do; the whirl appears after a turn and a half. Hint: { id: 'stir', text: 'stir the water with your hand', after: 160, ready: s.touchedWater, done: s.stirred } with s.stirred set by a 'stir' event. Carried lanterns are noticed by anyone stirring near one, which the reach placement makes likely.
conflicts: No pinch: a pinch ends the stir and hands locomotion the usual pull (the palm must be moving anyway, so the dead zone is passed honestly). Grab: unchanged; a stirring hand with a lantern in reach still grabs it on pinch. Leave: the hand is submerged, so the leave pose cannot be matched. Fireflies: submerged hands never recruit and the repel rule (speed > 0.7) still scatters at fast stirs. Lantern attraction requires !submerged, so the only lantern effect is the explicit eddy term. harnessStep: Add 'stir', 'stirend' to the eventLog list, 'speed' is already summarised; expose stats().stir = { strength, count }. Run before the lantern-star step (or after homing has brought a lantern within 1 m): const cx = 0.2, cz = -0.5, R = 0.12; pick the floating lantern nearest (cx, cz) from world() (lantern 0 sits ~0.33 m away at az 55 deg) and record az0 = atan2(lz - cz, lx - cx). For i = 0..108: a = 2*PI*i/72 (0.5 rev/s, palm speed ~0.38 m/s); setHand('right', [cx + R*cos(a), L - 0.15, cz + R*sin(a)], 0, { pitchDeg: -20, rollDeg: 0, curl: 0.3 }); frame(). Assert v = window.__nocturneCtx.stir.vortices[1]: v.s > 0.5, |v.omega| > 1.5 rad/s, hypot(v.x - cx, v.z - cz) < 0.1, and a 'stir' event with detail.hand === 'right'; then compare az1 for the same lantern: wrapPi(az1 - az0) * sign(v.omega) > 0.35 rad (the eddy carries it ~57 deg at 0.15 m/s; wind alone could account for at most ~22 deg and has no preferred sign). Step 'stir-unwinds': setHand('right', [0.25, L + 0.3, -0.45], 0); frames(150); assert v.s < 0.1 and a 'stirend' event.
risks: The weakest of the four: the sim already glows under a circling hand, so the whirl must earn its place through the motes and the carried lanterns; if the motes read as noise the count or size needs tuning. The centre estimate lags a moving circle by ~1 s, so an eddy drawn while wading drifts a little behind the hand. Lotus pads do not join the eddy (they are static in the sim's eyes), which a player stirring inside a cluster will notice; adding pad drift would be a small follow-up in lotus.js.
